summary: Deligne proves the Riemann hypothesis of the Weil conjectures: for a smooth projective variety X₀ over F_q the characteristic polynomial of geometric Frobenius on H^i(X, Q_ℓ) has integer coefficients independent of ℓ ≠ p, and all complex conjugates of its roots have absolute value q^{i/2} (Theorem 1.6, reduced in §1 to Lemma 1.7 by Grothendieck's cohomological rationality). §§1–2 recall Grothendieck's ℓ-adic theory: constructible and lisse Q_ℓ-sheaves, Frobenius conventions, the trace formula, L-functions of sheaves, Tate twists and Poincaré duality with the functional equation. §3 proves the fundamental estimate (3.2): a lisse sheaf on a curve with a symplectic pairing to Q_ℓ(−β), open symplectic monodromy and rational local factors is pure of weight β. The proof is Rankin's tensor-power positivity trick with the invariant theory of Sp. §§4–5 recall Picard–Lefschetz theory and Lefschetz pencils, including Kazhdan–Margulis openness of the monodromy (5.10). §6 proves rationality of the local factors of the radical quotient E/(E∩E^⊥) (6.2). §7 completes (1.7) by induction on dimension through a Lefschetz pencil and removes the error term by the tensor-power trick. §8 gives applications: point counts of complete intersections (8.1), the Ramanujan–Petersson conjecture (8.2), and Bombieri's bound (d−1)ⁿq^{n/2} for exponential sums of polynomials with smooth leading form (8.4). The atlas was built for this proof. DeligneWeightsAndPurity DWP.0–DWP.4 plan §§3, 6 and 7 almost step by step. LefschetzPencilsAndVanishingCycles LPV.0–LPV.5 plan the ℓ-adic Lefschetz theory. WeilConjectures WC.0–WC.3 and EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves EDC.1–EDC.4 plan the rationality, duality and final assembly. The §1 formalism is imported from the upstream CohomologicalPointCounting supplier through SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.2 and WC.0/WC.1. Of 208 items, 165 are planned, one is in the libraries (Tau Ceti's primitive forms with character, as needed in (8.2)) and 42 are missing. The 42 missing items are routed once: 41 to existing layers through five source routes, and the general GOS theorem to the outstanding shared étale-duality extension proposal with an explicit registration brief. The routes are: WC.1/WC.5 for the Hasse–Weil zeta function and the complete-intersection application; DWP.2/DWP.3 for four small inputs of §§3 and 6; LPV.0/LPV.2–LPV.4 for the complex model and trait recalls of §§4–5; FiniteFieldsAndCharacterSums FF.2 for the Artin–Schreier construction and applications in Bombieri's bound, importing general GOS from the shared étale-duality owner; and ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations R01.3 for the Artin–Schreier conductor computation. Route 6 coordinates that GOS proposal with the existing FF packet request instead of claiming the proposed EDC.2:euler-characteristic substage already exists. The P¹ constant-sheaf input is planned at early EDC.4, imported by both DWP.4 and DWP.6.

items.name: Hasse-Weil zeta function of a scheme of finite type over Z
items.statement: Let X be a scheme of finite type over Z, |X| the set of closed points of X and, for x in |X|, N(x) the number of elements of the residue field k(x). The Hasse-Weil zeta function of X is zeta_X(s) = prod_{x in |X|} (1 - N(x)^{-s})^{-1}; this product converges absolutely for Re(s) large enough. For X = Spec(Z), zeta_X(s) is the Riemann zeta function.
items.note: No scheme-level zeta function in Mathlib or Tau Ceti. The X=Spec(Z) case corresponds to Mathlib's Euler product riemannZeta_eulerProduct_tprod (Mathlib/NumberTheory/EulerProduct/DirichletLSeries.lean:98), but closed points of schemes with residue-field cardinalities and the general product/convergence are absent. WeilConjectures WC.6 explicitly excludes global Hasse-Weil L-functions over number fields. Motivational; the paper immediately restricts to schemes over F_q.

items.name: Zeta function Z(X;t) of a variety over F_q
items.statement: For X a scheme over the finite field F_q and x in |X|, write q_x = N(x); with deg(x) = [k(x):F_q] one has q_x = q^{deg(x)}. Put Z(X;t) = prod_{x in |X|} (1 - t^{deg(x)})^{-1}; this infinite product converges for |t| small enough, and zeta_X(s) = Z(X; q^{-s}) (1.1.3).
items.note: WC.1 ('Zeta arithmetic and finite-extension API'): 'Consume the coefficientwise Euler product and determinant formula. Expose integer coefficients, normalization at T=0 ...'; the WeilConjectures summary says 'The shared point-counting supplier constructs Z(X,T)=prod_{x in |X|}(1-T^deg(x))^{-1}=exp(sum N_r T^r/r)'. The raw construction is attributed to the PR196 point-counting supplier; WC.1 owns its public API. Library audit (WC.1): closed points of a scheme with their degrees are absent.

items.name: Rationality of the zeta function (Dwork, Grothendieck)
items.statement: (Dwork; Grothendieck [1] and SGA 5.) For X a scheme of finite type over F_q, Z(X,t) is a rational function of t. For Grothendieck this is a corollary of general results in l-adic cohomology (l a prime different from the characteristic p of F_q), which give a cohomological interpretation of the zeros and poles of Z(X;t), and a functional equation when X is proper and smooth.
items.note: WC.1: 'Recover rationality over Q from the actual integral point-count series and its cohomological rational realization, with a normalization ensuring uniqueness of coprime numerator and denominator.' Recalled result; the paper uses it through (1.5.4). The p-adic (Dwork, Berthelot, Lubkin) routes mentioned in the same paragraph are commentary only.

items.name: l-adic cohomology and cohomology with compact support of a variety
items.statement: Let X be an algebraic variety over an algebraically closed field k of characteristic p (i.e. a separated scheme of finite type over k; p = 0 is allowed). For every prime l != p, Grothendieck defined l-adic cohomology groups H^i(X, Q_l) and l-adic cohomology groups with proper support H^i_c(X, Q_l). For X proper the two coincide.
items.note: SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.2: 'construct sheaf cohomology, localization, proper/smooth base change and compact support. Integrate CohomologicalPointCounting suppliers'. Library audit SF.2: Mathlib defines H^i(X,Z_l) only as pro-etale cohomology of U -> C(U,Z_l); 'Missing: comparison with lim_n H^i_et(X,Z/l^n), Q_l coefficients, and constructible/lisse l-adic sheaves'. Compact support is not in either library.

items.name: Finiteness and vanishing of H^i_c(X,Q_l)
items.statement: For X an algebraic variety over an algebraically closed field k and l != char(k), the H^i_c(X, Q_l) are finite-dimensional Q_l-vector spaces, zero for i > 2 dim(X).

items.name: Frobenius morphism F : X -> X of a variety defined over F_q
items.statement: Let X_0 be an algebraic variety over F_q, F_q-bar an algebraic closure of F_q and X the variety over F_q-bar obtained from X_0 by extension of scalars. The Frobenius morphism F : X -> X sends the point with coordinates x to the point with coordinates x^q; equivalently, for U_0 a Zariski open of X_0 defining an open U of X, F^{-1}(U) = U and, for x in H^0(U_0, O), F^*x = x^q. Identify |X| with X_0(F_q-bar) = Hom_{F_q}(Spec(F_q-bar), X_0), and let phi in Gal(F_q-bar/F_q) be the Frobenius substitution phi(x) = x^q; the action of F on |X| is identified with the action of phi on X_0(F_q-bar).

Frobenius convention in every endpoint' and proves finite-type point finiteness, importing PR196 FrobeniusGeometry ('Finite-field points, Frobenius actions'). items.name: Fixed points of iterates of Frobenius are the F_{q^n}-rational points
items.statement: (a) The set X^F of closed points of X fixed by F identifies with the set X_0(F_q) subset X_0(F_q-bar) of points of X defined over F_q (for x in F_q-bar, x in F_q iff x^q = x). (b) Likewise, the set X^{F^n} of closed points of X fixed by the n-th iterate of F identifies with X_0(F_{q^n}).

WC.0 plans 'Register canonical translations between field-isomorphic point sets and compatibility with finite-extension towers' and finiteness of X(F_{q^r}), but not the fixed-point identification. items.name: Closed points of X_0 are Frobenius orbits; degree = orbit size
items.statement: The set |X_0| of closed points of X_0 identifies with the set |X|_F of orbits of F (or of phi) in |X|. The degree deg(x) of x in |X_0| is the number of elements of the corresponding orbit.
items.note: WC.1 plans the degree-m closed point count a_m and 'N_r=sum_{m|r} m a_m', which is proved via this orbit description. Library audit WC.1: 'Missing: closed points of a scheme with their degrees'.

items.name: N_n = sum over closed points of degree dividing n of their degree
items.statement: From (b) and (c): #X^{F^n} = #X_0(F_{q^n}) = sum_{x in |X_0|, deg(x) | n} deg(x) (for x in |X_0| with deg(x) | n, x defines deg(x) points with coordinates in F_{q^n}, all conjugate over F_q).
items.note: WC.1: 'Prove the relation N_r=sum_{m|r} m a_m, where a_m counts degree-m closed points, and the corresponding Mobius-inversion formula'. Library audit: Mobius inversion in Mathlib, the identity itself absent even for A^1.

items.name: Action F^* of Frobenius on H^i_c(X,Q_l)
items.statement: The morphism F is finite, in particular proper. It therefore induces maps F^* : H^i_c(X, Q_l) -> H^i_c(X, Q_l).

Those constructions are imported unchanged'). Needs functoriality of compact-support cohomology for proper maps, which is not in either library and is not an atlas stage deliverable.

items.name: Grothendieck-Lefschetz trace formula (constant coefficients)
items.statement: (Grothendieck) #X^F = sum_i (-1)^i Tr(F^*, H^i_c(X, Q_l)); the right side, a priori an l-adic number, is an integer equal to the left side. Such a formula is reasonable only because dF = 0, even at infinity (X is not assumed proper); dF = 0 implies the fixed points of F have multiplicity one. An analogous formula holds for the iterates of F: (1.5.1) #X^{F^n} = #X_0(F_{q^n}) = sum_i (-1)^i Tr(F^{*n}, H^i_c(X, Q_l)).

items.name: Logarithmic derivative of Z(X_0,t) is the point-count generating series
items.statement: Taking the logarithmic derivative of (1.1.2): t (d/dt) log Z(X_0,t) = (t (d/dt) Z(X_0,t)) / Z(X_0,t) = sum_{x in |X_0|} deg(x) t^{deg(x)} / (1 - t^{deg(x)}) = sum_{x in |X_0|} sum_{n>0} deg(x) t^{n deg(x)} = sum_n #X_0(F_{q^n}) t^n (by (1.4.1)).
items.note: WC summary: 'Z(X,T)=prod(1-T^deg(x))^{-1}=exp(sum_{r>=1} N_r T^r/r)'; WC.1 plans 'N_r=sum_{m|r} m a_m' and the Euler product API, from which this identity is the formal power series computation.

items.name: t d/dt log det(1-Ft)^{-1} = sum Tr(F^n) t^n
items.statement: For F an endomorphism of a (finite-dimensional) vector space V, one has the identity of formal series t (d/dt) log(det(1 - F t, V)^{-1}) = sum_{n>0} Tr(F^n, V) t^n. (Check it for dim(V) = 1 and observe that both sides are additive in V in a short exact sequence.)

items.name: Grothendieck's cohomological expression of Z(X_0,t)
items.statement: Substituting (1.5.1) in (1.5.2) and applying (1.5.3): t (d/dt) log Z(X_0,t) = sum_i (-1)^i t (d/dt) log det(1 - F^* t, H^i_c(X, Q_l))^{-1}, i.e. (1.5.4) Z(X_0,t) = prod_i det(1 - F^* t, H^i_c(X, Q_l))^{(-1)^{i+1}}. The right side is an element of Q_l(t); the formula asserts that its Taylor expansion at t = 0, a priori a formal series in Q_l[[t]] with constant term one, lies in Z[[t]] and equals the left side, also regarded as a formal series in t. This is Grothendieck's cohomological interpretation of the function Z.

items.name: Main theorem: Riemann hypothesis and integrality for smooth projective varieties
items.statement: Theorem (1.6). Let X_0 be a nonsingular (= smooth) projective variety over F_q. For each i, the characteristic polynomial det(t.1 - F^*, H^i(X, Q_l)) has integer coefficients independent of l (l != p). The complex roots alpha of this polynomial (the complex conjugates of the eigenvalues of F^*) have absolute value |alpha| = q^{i/2}.
items.note: WC.3 ('Integral factors, all-conjugates RH and l-independence'): 'Import DWP.4's proved purity ... Follow Deligne I (1.7)=>(1.6): begin with a reduced rational presentation ...; prove distinct cohomological weights prevent cancellation between the P_i; identify each factor by the absolute values of its roots. Establish Galois stability over Q and integrality ... Prove that this characterization is independent of l.' The main result of the paper.

items.name: Lemma 1.7: eigenvalues of Frobenius on H^i are algebraic of weight i
items.statement: Lemma (1.7). For each i and each l != p, the eigenvalues of the endomorphism F^* of H^i(X, Q_l) (X_0 smooth projective over F_q as in (1.6)) are algebraic numbers all of whose complex conjugates alpha have absolute value |alpha| = q^{i/2}.
items.note: DWP.4: 'Export Weil I Lemma1.7 for every smooth projective X_0'; '§1.6-1.7 supplies the WC handoff'. The rest of the paper (§§3-7) proves (1.7).

items.name: Z(X_0,t) is in Z[[t]] ∩ Q_l(t), hence in Q(t) (Hankel determinants)
items.statement: Regard Z(X_0,t) as a formal series with constant term 1 in Z[[t]]: Z(X_0,t) = sum_n a_n t^n. By (1.5.4) its image in Q_l[[t]] is the Taylor expansion of a rational function. This means that for N and M large enough (>= the degrees of numerator and denominator) the Hankel determinants H_k = det((a_{i+j+k})_{0<=i,j<=M}) (k > N) vanish. This vanishing holds in Q_l iff it holds in Q; so Z(X_0,t) is the Taylor expansion of an element of Q(t): Z(X_0,t) in Z[[t]] ∩ Q_l(t) ⊂ Q(t).
items.note: WC.1: 'Recover rationality over Q from the actual integral point-count series and its cohomological rational realization ... Record the Fatou/Gauss and rational-descent lemmas needed later.' The Hankel-determinant (Kronecker) criterion is not in Mathlib or Tau Ceti (searched declarations.tsv for Hankel/Kronecker).

items.name: Fatou's lemma: normalized integral rational series has numerator and denominator with constant term 1
items.statement: Write Z(X_0,t) = P/Q with P, Q in Z[t] coprime and with positive constant term. By a lemma of Fatou, since Z(X_0,t) is in Z[[t]] with constant term one, the constant terms of P and Q are 1.
items.note: WC.1: 'Record the Fatou/Gauss and rational-descent lemmas needed later.' Library audit WC.1: 'Fatou's lemma for rational power series is absent'.

items.name: (1.7) implies (1.6): identification, rationality, integrality and l-independence of P_i
items.statement: Put P_i(t) = det(1 - F^* t, H^i(X, Q_l)). By hypothesis (1.7) the P_i are pairwise coprime, so the right side of (1.5.4) is in irreducible form and P(t) = prod_{i odd} P_i(t), Q(t) = prod_{i even} P_i(t). Let K be the subfield of an algebraic closure Q_l-bar of Q_l generated over Q by the roots of R(t) = P(t)Q(t). The roots of P_i(t) are those roots of R(t) all of whose complex conjugates have absolute value q^{-i/2}; this set is stable under Gal(K/Q), so P_i(t) has rational coefficients. By Gauss's lemma (or because the roots of P_i, being roots of R(t), are inverses of algebraic integers) it even has integer coefficients. The description of the roots of P_i(t) is independent of l, so the polynomial P_i(t) itself is independent of l.
items.note: WC.3: 'prove distinct cohomological weights prevent cancellation between the P_i; identify each factor by the absolute values of its roots. Establish Galois stability over Q and integrality by the normalized rational-function/Gauss argument. Prove that this characterization is independent of l.' Mathlib has Gauss's lemma for polynomials over a GCD domain (library audit WC.1).

items.name: Constructible Q_l-sheaves (Q_l-faisceaux)
items.statement: Let X be an algebraic variety over a field k. For the definition of a constructible Q_l-sheaf on X see SGA 5 VI. (a) If F is a constructible Q_l-sheaf on X, there is a finite partition of X into locally closed parts X_i such that F|X_i is twisted constant (constant tordu, i.e. lisse). Only constructible Q_l-sheaves are considered, and they are simply called Q_l-sheaves.

items.statement: Suppose X connected and let x-bar be a geometric point of X. items.name: Constructible Q_l-sheaves over C are analytic sheaves with Z_l-local-system strata
items.statement: If k = C, the constructible Q_l-sheaves on X identify with the sheaves of Q_l-vector spaces F on X^an for which there is a finite partition of X into Zariski-locally closed parts X_i and, for each i, a local system of free finite-type Z_l-modules F_i on X_i with F|X_i = F_i ⊗_{Z_l} Q_l. items.name: Canonical isomorphism F^*: F^* F -> F for a sheaf defined over F_q
items.statement: Let X_0 be an algebraic variety over F_q, X the corresponding variety over F_q-bar, F_0 a sheaf of sets on X_0 (etale topology) and F its inverse image on X. Besides the Frobenius morphism F : X -> X there is a canonical isomorphism F^* : F^*F -> F, described as follows: regard F_0 as an etale space [F_0] over X_0 with etale f : [F_0] -> X_0 such that F_0 is the sheaf of local sections; [F] is deduced from [F_0] by extension of scalars, giving a commutative square (Frobenius of [F] over Frobenius of X), whence a morphism [F] -> X ×_{(F,X,f)} [F] = [F^*F], which is an isomorphism because f is etale; its inverse defines F^*: F^*F -> F. This construction generalizes to Q_l-sheaves.

items.name: Frobenius endomorphism F^* of H^i_c(X,F) and local Frobenius F_x^*
items.statement: Let X_0 be an algebraic variety over F_q, F_0 a Q_l-sheaf on X_0, (X, F) deduced by extension of scalars to F_q-bar, F : X -> X and F^* : F^*F -> F. The finite morphism F and F^* define an endomorphism F^* : H^i_c(X, F) -> H^i_c(X, F^*F) -> H^i_c(X, F). For x in |X|, F^* defines a morphism F^*_x : F_{F(x)} -> F_x; for x in X^F it is an endomorphism of F_x. The n-th iterate of F^* defines morphisms F^{*n}_x : F_{F^n(x)} -> F_x; for x fixed under F^n, F^{*n}_x is an endomorphism.

items.name: Orientation sheaf and fundamental class (differentiable and complex manifolds); Z(1)
items.statement: (a) Let X be a differentiable manifold of pure dimension n. The orientation sheaf Z' on X is the sheaf locally isomorphic to the constant sheaf Z whose invertible sections over an open U correspond to orientations of U; an orientation of X is an isomorphism of Z' with the constant sheaf Z. The fundamental class of X is a morphism Tr : H^n_c(X, Z') -> Z; if X is oriented it identifies with Tr : H^n_c(X, Z) -> Z; Poincaré duality is expressed using the fundamental class. (b) Let C be an algebraic closure of R. A smooth complex algebraic variety (its underlying differentiable manifold) is always orientable; to orient it it suffices to orient C, i.e. to choose one of the roots +i of X^2 = -1, equivalently an isomorphism of R/Z with U^1 = {z in C : |z| = 1} (+i is the image of 1/4), equivalently one of the two isomorphisms x -> exp(±2πix) of Q/Z with the group of roots of unity of C. Z(1) denotes a free Z-module of rank one whose two-element set of generators is in canonical correspondence with these choices; simplest is Z(1) = Ker(exp : C -> C^*), the generator y = ±2πi corresponding to x -> exp(xy). Z(r) is the r-th tensor power of Z(1). If X is a smooth complex algebraic variety of pure complex dimension r, its orientation sheaf is the constant sheaf with value Z(r).
items.note: The Tau Ceti AlgebraicTopology stage 6 constructs local orientation classes and the orientation local system of a manifold, with Poincaré duality by cap product (as recorded in the reviewed audit of ArithmeticLocallySymmetricSpaces ALS.0). Motivational, restating classical cases 'dans un langage farfelu'. Mathlib: Complex.exp_eq_one_iff (Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Complex/Log.lean:142: exp x = 1 iff x = n·(2πI)) gives Ker(exp) = Z·2πi, but orientation sheaves, fundamental class and topological Poincaré duality in this form are absent and not planned by the l-adic roadmaps.

items.name: Tate module Z_l(1), Q_l(1) and Tate twists Q_l(r)
items.statement: To 'orient' algebraic varieties over an algebraically closed field k of characteristic 0 one must choose an isomorphism of Q/Z with the group of roots of unity of k; these form a principal homogeneous space under Z-hat^* (no longer Z^*). For l-adic cohomology it suffices to consider roots of unity of l-power order, assuming the characteristic p of k different from l. Z/l^n(1) is the group of roots of unity of k of order dividing l^n; for varying n these form a projective system with transition maps sigma_{m,n} : Z/l^m(1) -> Z/l^n(1), x -> x^{l^{m-n}}. Put Z_l(1) = lim proj Z/l^n(1) and Q_l(1) = Z_l(1) ⊗_{Z_l} Q_l. Q_l(r) is the r-th tensor power of Q_l(1); for r in Z negative, put Q_l(r) = Q_l(-r)^∨ (dual).

Mathlib has rootsOfUnity and the Z_p^*-valued cyclotomicCharacter (Mathlib/NumberTheory/Cyclotomic/CyclotomicCharacter.lean:307) but no Tate module Z_l(1) as a Galois module.

However the group of automorphisms of k acts nontrivially on Q_l(1): it acts via the Z_l^*-valued character giving its action on roots of unity. In particular, if k = F_q-bar, the Frobenius substitution phi : x -> x^q acts by multiplication by q.

Partially in Mathlib: cyclotomicCharacter (Mathlib/NumberTheory/Cyclotomic/CyclotomicCharacter.lean:307) with cyclotomicCharacter.spec (line 323: g t = t^(chi(g) mod p^n) for p^n-th roots of unity t); but neither the module Q_l(1) nor the value chi(phi) = q for the Frobenius of F_q-bar is stated. DWP.0 plans weights of 'Tate twists' (and DWP.10 the acceptance example 'Q_l(1) with weight -2') but not this action itself.

items.name: l-adic orientation sheaf Q_l(n) and trace (fundamental class) Tr: H^{2n}_c(X,Q_l(n)) -> Q_l
items.statement: Let X be a smooth algebraic variety of pure dimension n over k (algebraically closed, char != l). The orientation sheaf of X in l-adic cohomology is the constant Q_l-sheaf Q_l(n). The fundamental class is a morphism Tr : H^{2n}_c(X, Q_l(n)) -> Q_l, or equivalently Tr : H^{2n}_c(X, Q_l) -> Q_l(-n).
items.note: EDC.2:trace-purity: 'Construct Tr_f:Rf_!Λ(d)[2d]->Λ for smooth pure relative dimension d and prove that its adjoint f^*Λ(d)[2d]->f^!Λ is an isomorphism ... The normalization is fixed by degree-one closed points and c_1(O(1)) on P^1.' Paper cites SGA 4 XVIII.

items.name: Poincaré duality for smooth proper varieties (constant coefficients)
items.statement: Theorem (2.3) (Poincaré duality). For X proper and smooth of pure dimension n (over k algebraically closed, l != char k), the bilinear form Tr(x ∪ y) : H^i(X, Q_l) ⊗ H^{2n-i}(X, Q_l) -> Q_l(-n) is a perfect duality (it identifies H^i(X, Q_l) with the dual of H^{2n-i}(X, Q_l(n))).
items.note: EDC.2:pairings: 'For smooth separated finite-type X/k, deduce the perfect pairing H_c^i(X_bar,E)×H^(2d-i)(X_bar,E(d))->E; for proper X remove compact support.' Paper cites SGA 4 XVIII (2.14 B).

items.name: Frobenius eigenvalues on H^{2n-i} are q^n/alpha_j
items.statement: Let X_0 be a proper smooth algebraic variety over F_q, of pure dimension n, and X over F_q-bar deduced by extension of scalars. The morphism (2.3) is compatible with the action of Gal(F_q-bar/F_q). Hence, if (alpha_j) are the eigenvalues of the geometric Frobenius F acting on H^i(X, Q_l), the eigenvalues of F acting on H^{2n-i}(X, Q_l) are the (q^n alpha_j^{-1}).
items.note: WC.2: 'Use the actual Frobenius-equivariant pairing H^i⊗H^{2d-i}->Q_l(-d), with geometric Frobenius acting by q^d on the target. Derive b_i=b_{2d-i}, invertibility of F, reciprocal eigenvalue pairing and the polynomial reciprocity identity'. Galois equivariance of the pairing: EDC.2:pairings ('Prove graded symmetry and Frobenius/Galois equivariance, giving <Fx,Fy>=q^d<x,y>'); linear algebra: DWP.0 ('the reciprocal pairing of eigenvalues induced by a Frobenius-equivariant perfect pairing'). Library audit WC.2/EDC.8: only the unscaled charpoly(A^{-1}) reversal is in Mathlib.

items.name: Geometric form of (2.4): F^* is multiplication by q^n on H^{2n}
items.statement: Assume X connected. (a) Cup product puts H^i(X, Q_l) and H^{2n-i}(X, Q_l) in perfect duality with values in H^{2n}(X, Q_l), which is one-dimensional. (b) Cup product commutes with the inverse image F^* by the Frobenius morphism F : X -> X. (c) The morphism F is finite of degree q^n: on H^{2n}(X, Q_l), F^* is multiplication by q^n. (d) Hence the eigenvalues of F^* have property (2.4).
items.note: EDC.2:pairings: 'Prove graded symmetry and Frobenius/Galois equivariance, giving <Fx,Fy>=q^d<x,y> in the untwisted top-degree convention.' The degree-q^n statement for the finite morphism F uses the finite-flat trace of EDC.2:trace-purity ('Build the trace for finite flat relative-dimension-zero maps with degree and base-change compatibility').

items.name: Euler characteristic and parity of n·chi(X)
items.statement: Put chi(X) = sum_i (-1)^i dim H^i(X, Q_l). If n is odd, the form Tr(x ∪ y) on H^n(X, Q_l) is alternating; hence the integer n·chi(X) is always even.
items.note: WC.2: 'derive the usual ±q^{dχ/2} formulation with a defined sign and the needed parity statement ... Odd middle degree uses the alternating pairing; in characteristic-zero coefficients this also controls evenness of its dimension, including at l=2.' Library audit WC.2: evenness of alternating nondegenerate forms over a general field is absent (Tau Ceti has only the real symplectic case).

items.name: Functional equation of Z(X_0,t) (Grothendieck's formulation)
items.statement: For X_0 proper and smooth over F_q of pure dimension n, one deduces easily from (1.5.4), (2.3) and (2.4) that Z(X_0, t) = ε · q^{-n chi(X)/2} · t^{-chi(X)} · Z(X_0, q^{-n} t^{-1}), where ε = ±1. If n is even, let N be the multiplicity of the eigenvalue q^{n/2} of F^* acting on H^n(X, Q_l) (i.e. the dimension of the corresponding generalized eigenspace). Then ε = 1 if n is odd and ε = (-1)^N if n is even.
items.note: WC.2 ('Poincaré duality and exact functional equation'): 'prove Z(X,1/(q^dT))=(-1)^χ Δ T^χ Z(X,T), Δ^2=q^{dχ} ... then derive the usual ±q^{dχ/2} formulation with a defined sign'. EDC.8 exports 'the determinant relation ... tracking the middle-degree determinant and Koszul sign'. The sign formula was checked by hand: pairs alpha, q^n/alpha contribute positively; for n even det(F|H^n) = (-1)^{N_-} q^{n b_n/2} and b_n ≡ N_+ + N_- mod 2, giving ε = (-1)^{N_+}, N_+ = multiplicity of +q^{n/2}, as printed.

items.name: Twist F(r) = F ⊗ Q_l(r) of a Q_l-sheaf
items.statement: If F is a Q_l-sheaf on an algebraic variety X over k algebraically closed, F(r) denotes the sheaf F ⊗ Q_l(r). This sheaf is (non-canonically) isomorphic to F.
items.note: DWP.0 and R34.1 own the 'elementary tensor/dual/twist rules' for weights (R34.1: 'Import DWP.0's Weil numbers, ... and elementary tensor/dual/twist rules'). Mathlib has the cyclotomic character of a field (`cyclotomicCharacter`), the Galois action on Z_ℓ(1). Tate twists of sheaves are attributed to the external ConstructibleEtale owner (EDC summary); no atlas stage constructs them.

items.name: Poincaré duality for a lisse sheaf on a smooth variety
items.statement: Theorem (2.8). Suppose X smooth of pure dimension n and F twisted constant (lisse). Let F^∨ be the dual of F. The bilinear form Tr(x ∪ y) : H^i(X, F) ⊗ H^{2n-i}_c(X, F^∨(n)) -> H^{2n}_c(X, F ⊗ F^∨(n)) -> H^{2n}_c(X, Q_l(n)) -> Q_l is a perfect duality.
items.note: EDC.1:biduality: 'Derive the relative duality comparison Ra_*D_X K≅RHom(Ra_!K,Λ) in D(k_et). After geometric base change this gives RΓ(X_bar,D_Xbar K_bar)≅RHom(RΓ_c(X_bar,K_bar),Λ)', combined with EDC.2:trace-purity's identification f^*Λ(d)[2d]≅f^!Λ, which for lisse F gives D F = F^∨(n)[2n]; EDC.2:pairings deduces the cohomological perfect pairings. Paper cites SGA 4 XVIII.

items.name: H^0(X,F) = invariants of pi_1 on the fibre
items.statement: Suppose X connected and let x be a closed point of X. The functor F -> F_x is an equivalence of the category of twisted constant Q_l-sheaves with that of l-adic representations of pi_1(X, x). Via this equivalence, H^0(X, F) identifies with the invariants of pi_1(X, x) acting on F_x: (2.9.1) H^0(X, F) ≅ F_x^{pi_1(X,x)}.
items.note: Planned under the atlas convention for the upstream CohomologicalPointCounting (PR196) suppliers, which have no atlas stage of their own: SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2 'Integrate[s] CohomologicalPointCounting suppliers' (sheaf cohomology, base change, compact support) and WeilConjectures WC.0/WC.1 reconcile and consume them (WC.1: 'Consume the coefficientwise Euler product and determinant formula'; its requires list names UPSTREAM:CohomologicalPointCounting:TraceFormula). Same decision as the accepted extractions PAPER-SCHMIDT-STIX-16, PAPER-BERGSTROM-FABER-PAYNE-24 and PAPER-LIU-WOOD-ZUREICKBROWN-24. EDC.0 imports 'the actual bounded constructible/ctf subcategories'. Not planned by any atlas stage: the atlas attributes this to the external pinned 'PR196' CohomologicalPointCounting family (ConstructibleEtale / EtaleBaseChange / CompactSupport / EllAdicRealization / TraceFormula), which has no atlas stage ids (see EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves summary: 'TraceFormula owns perfect-complex traces and Frobenius point counting. Those constructions are imported unchanged'). Needs the etale fundamental group and lisse sheaves (absent). Not planned in an atlas stage.

items.name: H^{2n}_c(X,F) = coinvariants of pi_1 twisted by (-n)
items.statement: By (2.8), for X smooth and connected of dimension n and F twisted constant: H^{2n}_c(X, F) = H^0(X, F^∨(n))^∨ = ((F_x^∨(n))^{pi_1(X,x)})^∨. Duality exchanges invariants (largest invariant subspace) and coinvariants (largest invariant quotient), so H^{2n}_c(X, F) = (F_x)_{pi_1(X,x)}(-n). (Used only for n = 1.)
items.note: DWP.2: 'Use Poincaré duality to calculate H^2_c of these tensor powers' (the n = 1, U open in P^1 case, which is the only use). No stage plans the general-n formula as such.

items.name: Scholie: H^0_c and H^2_c of a lisse sheaf on a smooth connected curve
items.statement: Scholie (2.10). Let X be a smooth connected curve over k algebraically closed, x a closed point of X and F a twisted constant Q_l-sheaf. Then (i) H^0_c(X, F) = 0 if X is affine; (ii) H^2_c(X, F) = (F_x)_{pi_1(X,x)}(-1). Assertion (i) means simply that F has no section with finite support.
items.note: (ii): DWP.2 'Use Poincaré duality to calculate H^2_c of these tensor powers'. (i) is not explicitly planned; it is elementary once H_c and lisse sheaves exist. Used in §3 (3.4-3.5).

items.name: Stalks of j_*F at boundary points are local monodromy invariants
items.statement: Let X be a projective, smooth, connected curve over k algebraically closed, U an open of X, complement of a finite set S of closed points, j the inclusion U -> X and F a twisted constant Q_l-sheaf on U. Let j_*F be the constructible Q_l-sheaf direct image of F. Its fibre at x in S has rank at most the rank of its fibre at a general point; it is a space of invariants under a local monodromy group.
items.note: DWP.6 works with j_* of pure lisse sheaves on curves (the duality (2.12) item is planned there); LPV.1 owns inertia and local monodromy. Not planned by any atlas stage: the atlas attributes this to the external pinned 'PR196' CohomologicalPointCounting family (ConstructibleEtale / EtaleBaseChange / CompactSupport / EllAdicRealization / TraceFormula), which has no atlas stage ids (see EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves summary: 'TraceFormula owns perfect-complex traces and Frobenius point counting. Those constructions are imported unchanged'). LPV.1 constructs inertia/local monodromy, and DWP.5 studies 'the weights of boundary invariants of j_*F', but no stage states this stalk description.

items.name: Poincaré duality for j_*F on a projective smooth curve
items.statement: Theorem (2.12). In the situation of (2.11), the bilinear form Tr(x ∪ y) : H^i(X, j_*F) ⊗ H^{2-i}(X, j_*F^∨(1)) -> H^2(X, j_*F ⊗ j_*F^∨(1)) -> H^2(X, j_*(F ⊗ F^∨)(1)) -> H^2(X, j_*Q_l(1)) = H^2(X, Q_l(1)) -> Q_l is a perfect duality.
items.note: DWP.6: 'Prove the correct duality for j_*F; do not substitute Rj_*F without its boundary comparison.' Also consumed in Weil I §3 via DWP.2 (Cor. 3.9 for H^1(P^1,j_*F)). Per 2.14 E it follows from SGA 4 XVIII (3.2.5) (S = Spec(k), K = j_*F, L = Q_l) by a local computation; EDC.1:biduality supplies that general theorem.

items.name: Tate sheaves Z/l^n(1), Q_l(r) on a scheme where l is invertible
items.statement: It is convenient to have the Q_l-sheaves Q_l(r) on any scheme X on which l is invertible. It suffices to define the Z/l^n(1): by definition Z/l^n(1) is the etale sheaf of (l^n)-th roots of unity.
items.note: DWP.0 and R34.1 own the 'elementary tensor/dual/twist rules' for weights (R34.1: 'Import DWP.0's Weil numbers, ... and elementary tensor/dual/twist rules'). Mathlib has the cyclotomic character of a field (`cyclotomicCharacter`), the Galois action on Z_ℓ(1). Owned by the external ConstructibleEtale family ('Tate twists', EDC summary); no atlas stage. Mathlib has no mu_{l^n} as an etale sheaf (library audit SF.2: 'Missing: ... constant torsion coefficient sheaves Z/n, Kummer/Artin-Schreier sequences').

items.name: Setting of §3: open curve U₀ ⊂ P¹ over F_q with a lisse Q_ℓ-sheaf
items.statement: Let U₀ be a curve over F_q which is the complement in P¹ of a finite set of closed points, U the curve over F̄_q deduced from it, u a closed point of U, F₀ a twisted-constant (i.e. lisse) Q_ℓ-sheaf on U₀ and F its inverse image on U.
items.note: DWP.2: "Here U₀ is an open of ℙ¹ over k₀, F₀ is a nonzero lisse ℚ_ℓ-sheaf, it has a nondegenerate alternating pairing F₀⊗F₀→ℚ_ℓ(−β) for β∈ℤ, its **geometric** monodromy image is open in the corresponding symplectic group, and every local polynomial det(1−T F_x,F₀) has rational coefficients. Prove that F₀ is punctually pure of weight β." This is the standing setting for (3.2)–(3.9).

items.name: Weight β of a lisse sheaf (Weil I sense)
items.statement: Let β∈Q. F₀ is said to be of weight β if for every x∈|U₀| the eigenvalues of F_x acting on F₀ (1.13) are algebraic numbers all of whose complex conjugates have absolute value q_x^{β/2}.
items.note: DWP.0: "Define Weil q-numbers of an integer weight on actual algebraic-number carriers and their all-embeddings absolute-value property." The sheaf-level predicate ("punctually pure of weight β") is the conclusion of DWP.2. Note the paper allows β∈Q here; DWP.0 plans integer weights for Weil numbers and a separate real-weight ι-predicate.

items.name: Q_ℓ(r) has weight −2r
items.statement: For example, Q_ℓ(r) is of weight −2r.
items.note: DWP.0: "Prove ... products, duals, tensor powers, Tate twists and finite-field base extension"; DWP.10 acceptance lists "ℚ_ℓ(1) with weight−2". Used to read off weights of Q_ℓ(−kβ−1) in (3.7).

items.name: Fundamental estimate (Théorème 3.2)
items.statement: Assume: (i) F₀ is equipped with a nondegenerate alternating bilinear form ψ: F₀⊗F₀ → Q_ℓ(−β) (β∈Z); (ii) the image of π₁(U,u) in GL(F_u) is an open subgroup of the symplectic group Sp(F_u, ψ_u); (iii) for every x∈|U₀|, the polynomial det(1−F_x t, F₀) has rational coefficients. Then F is of weight β [i.e. F₀ is of weight β in the sense of (3.1)].
items.note: DWP.2: "Here U₀ is an open of ℙ¹ over k₀, F₀ is a nonzero lisse ℚ_ℓ-sheaf, it has a nondegenerate alternating pairing F₀⊗F₀→ℚ_ℓ(−β) for β∈ℤ, its **geometric** monodromy image is open in the corresponding symplectic group, and every local polynomial det(1−T F_x,F₀) has rational coefficients. Prove that F₀ is punctually pure of weight β." Note π₁(U,u) is the geometric fundamental group (U over F̄_q). This is the main result of §3; applied in §6 (Corollaire 6.3) to the radical quotient of vanishing cycles of a pencil.

items.name: Reduction: U affine and F ≠ 0
items.statement: In proving (3.2) one may assume, and we shall assume, that U is affine and that F ≠ 0.
items.note: DWP.2: "Here U₀ is an open of ℙ¹ over k₀, F₀ is a nonzero lisse ℚ_ℓ-sheaf, it has a nondegenerate alternating pairing F₀⊗F₀→ℚ_ℓ(−β) for β∈ℤ, its **geometric** monodromy image is open in the corresponding symplectic group, and every local polynomial det(1−T F_x,F₀) has rational coefficients. Prove that F₀ is punctually pure of weight β." (the atlas statement already takes F₀ nonzero). Trivial reduction: F=0 is vacuous, and removing one more rational point from U₀ changes neither hypotheses nor conclusion at the remaining points; affineness is needed for H⁰_c=0 in (3.7).

items.name: Lemma 3.3: log-derivative of local factor of even tensor power has nonnegative rational coefficients
items.statement: Let 2k be an even integer and denote by ⊗^{2k}F₀ the (2k)-th tensor power of F₀. For x∈|U₀|, the logarithmic derivative t (d/dt) log(det(1 − F_x t^{deg(x)}, ⊗^{2k}F₀)^{−1}) is a formal series with positive (i.e. ≥0) rational coefficients. Proof: by (iii), Tr(F_x^n, F₀)∈Q for all n; hence Tr(F_x^n, ⊗^{2k}F₀) = Tr(F_x^n, F₀)^{2k} is a nonnegative rational, and one applies (1.5.3).
items.note: DWP.2: "Construct the even tensor-power argument: local trace powers are rational and nonnegative after complex embedding; logarithmic derivatives and exponentiation give nonnegative local Euler-factor coefficients." Uses (1.5.3) (from §1).

items.name: Trace on a tensor power is the power of the trace
items.statement: For an endomorphism F of a finite-dimensional vector space V, Tr(F^n, ⊗^{2k}V) = Tr(F^n, V)^{2k}; in particular, if Tr(F^n,V)∈Q this is a nonnegative rational number.
items.note: DWP.0 plans "tensor/dual spectra" and "tensor powers". Mathlib has the binary case LinearMap.trace_tensorProduct' (Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Trace.lean:258: trace (map f g) = trace f * trace g, read), but not the iterated tensor-power statement itself, so not marked library.

items.name: Lemma 3.4: local factors of even tensor power have nonnegative rational coefficients
items.statement: The local factors det(1 − F_x t^{deg(x)}, ⊗^{2k}F₀)^{−1} are formal series with positive (≥0) rational coefficients. Proof: the formal series log det(1 − F_x t^{deg(x)}, ⊗^{2k}F₀)^{−1} has no constant term; by (3.3) its coefficients are ≥0; hence the coefficients of its exponential are also ≥0.
items.note: DWP.2: "logarithmic derivatives and exponentiation give nonnegative local Euler-factor coefficients."

items.name: Lemma 3.5: factors of a positive infinite product have radius at least that of the product
items.statement: Let f_i = Σ_n a_{i,n} t^n be a sequence of formal series with constant term 1 and nonnegative real coefficients. Assume the order of f_i − 1 tends to infinity with i, and put f = Π_i f_i. Then the radius of absolute convergence of f_i is at least that of f. Proof: if f = Σ_n a_n t^n, then a_{i,n} ≤ a_n.
items.note: DWP.2: "Prove the positive-series coefficient/radius-of-convergence and meromorphic-pole lemmas used in §§3.3–3.6." Nothing in Mathlib/Tau Ceti states this (searched declarations index for radius/Pringsheim).

items.name: Lemma 3.6: nearest pole of the product is no farther than nearest pole of a factor
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of (3.5), if f and the f_i are the Taylor expansions of meromorphic functions, then inf{|z| : f(z)=∞} ≤ inf{|z| : f_i(z)=∞}. Proof: these numbers are the radii of absolute convergence.
items.note: DWP.2: "Prove the positive-series coefficient/radius-of-convergence and meromorphic-pole lemmas used in §§3.3–3.6." Uses that the Taylor series at 0 of a meromorphic function on C holomorphic at 0 has radius equal to the modulus of the nearest pole.

items.name: Contraction forms ψ_P attached to pairings of [1,2k]
items.statement: For each partition P of [1,2k] into two-element parts {i_α, j_α} (i_α<j_α), define ψ_P : ⊗^{2k}F₀ → Q_ℓ(−kβ) : x₁⊗…⊗x_{2k} ↦ Π_α ψ(x_{i_α}, x_{j_α}).
items.note: DWP.2: "Prove the symplectic tensor invariant/coinvariant calculation by contraction pairings".

items.name: Open subgroup of Sp(Q_ℓ) is Zariski dense; coinvariants agree
items.statement: Hypothesis (ii) ensures that the coinvariants of π₁(U,u) in ⊗^{2k}F_u are the coinvariants in ⊗^{2k}F_u of the whole symplectic group (π₁ is Zariski-dense in Sp).
items.note: DWP.2 plans the Sp coinvariant calculation and LPV.5 openness, but no stage plans the step "an open subgroup of Sp(V)(Q_ℓ) is Zariski dense in Sp(V), so its coinvariants on an algebraic representation equal those of Sp". Searched atlas for "Zariski dens": only unrelated hits (LPV.5 explicitly contrasts open vs Zariski dense). Could be absorbed in DWP.2.

items.name: Invariant theory of Sp (H. Weyl): coinvariants of ⊗^{2k} via ψ_P
items.statement: Let 𝒫 be the set of partitions P. By H. Weyl (The classical groups, Ch. VI §1), for a suitable 𝒫'⊂𝒫 depending on dim(F_u), the ψ_P for P∈𝒫' define an isomorphism (⊗^{2k}F_u)_{π₁} = (⊗^{2k}F_u)_{Sp} ≅ Q_ℓ(−kβ)^{𝒫'}.
items.note: DWP.2: "Prove the symplectic tensor invariant/coinvariant calculation by contraction pairings (the required finite-rank invariant theory belongs here unless already available from the representation owner)." Related: tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/RepresentationTheory/SchurWeyl#layer-9-schur-weyl-duality-for-the-orthogonal-and-symplectic-groups-the-brauer-algebra plans "brauerActionSymp_surjective_to_commutant" (first fundamental theorem for Sp) but only over ℂ with Matrix.symplecticGroup; Deligne needs it over Q_ℓ. Not in libraries.

items.name: H²_c of the even tensor power
items.statement: Let N be the number of elements of 𝒫'. By (2.10), H²_c(U, ⊗^{2k}F) ≅ Q_ℓ(−kβ−1)^N.
items.note: DWP.2: "Use Poincaré duality to calculate H²_c of these tensor powers". Uses (2.10) (H²_c(U,G) = (G_u)_{π₁}(−1), from §2).

items.name: H⁰_c vanishes on an affine curve
items.statement: H⁰_c(U, ⊗^{2k}F) = 0 (U affine).
items.note: Standard (no compactly supported sections of a lisse sheaf on a non-proper connected curve). No atlas stage phrase found planning it explicitly (DWP.2 depends on "PR196 TraceFormula Layers11/14 and compact support"); searched atlas for H⁰_c. Used to reduce (1.14.3) to the displayed Z formula.

items.name: Zeta function of the even tensor power
items.statement: Formula (1.14.3) reduces to Z(U₀, ⊗^{2k}F₀, t) = det(1 − F*t, H¹_c(U, ⊗^{2k}F)) / (1 − q^{kβ+1}t)^N. This Z is therefore the Taylor expansion of a rational function whose only poles are at t = 1/q^{kβ+1}; only the fact that the poles have absolute value 1/q^{kβ+1} in C will be used.
items.note: DWP.2: "the actual trace formula to locate possible global poles". Printed H¹ without subscript c (PAPER-DELIGNE-74/E3). Uses (1.14.3) (Grothendieck trace formula, §1).

items.name: Eigenvalues of the tensor power
items.statement: If α is an eigenvalue of F_x on F₀, then α^{2k} is an eigenvalue of F_x on ⊗^{2k}F₀.
items.note: DWP.0: "Prove ... tensor/dual spectra".

items.name: Upper bound |α| ≤ q_x^{β/2}
items.statement: Let α be (any complex conjugate of) an eigenvalue of F_x on F₀. The inverse power 1/α^{2k/deg(x)} is a pole of det(1 − F_x t^{deg(x)}, ⊗^{2k}F)^{−1}; by (3.4) and (3.6), |1/q^{kβ+1}| ≤ |1/α^{2k/deg(x)}|, i.e. |α| ≤ q_x^{β/2 + 1/(2k)}. Letting k→∞, |α| ≤ q_x^{β/2}.
items.note: DWP.2: "Establish the resulting bound with an error tending to zero as the tensor power grows".

items.name: Lower bound via the pairing
items.statement: The existence of ψ ensures that q_x^β α^{−1} is also an eigenvalue of F_x on F₀, whence |q_x^β α^{−1}| ≤ q_x^{β/2}, i.e. q_x^{β/2} ≤ |α|. This completes the proof of (3.2).
items.note: DWP.2: "reciprocal eigenvalues from the pairing give the lower bound"; DWP.0: "the reciprocal pairing of eigenvalues induced by a Frobenius-equivariant perfect pairing".

items.name: Corollary 3.8: coarse upper bound on H¹_c
items.statement: [Under the hypotheses of (3.2).] Let α be an eigenvalue of F* acting on H¹_c(U,F). Then α is an algebraic number all of whose complex conjugates satisfy |α| ≤ q^{(β+1)/2 + 1/2}.
items.note: DWP.2: "Prove Corollaries3.8–3.9 with their **coarse**, not final Weil II, weight intervals for H¹_c(U,F) and H¹(ℙ¹,j_*F)."

items.name: Z(U₀,F₀,t) = det(1 − F*t, H¹_c(U,F))
items.statement: Formula (1.14.3) for F₀ reduces to Z(U₀,F₀,t) = det(1 − F*t, H¹_c(U,F)) [since H⁰_c = 0 (U affine) and H²_c = (F_u)_{π₁}(−1) = 0 by (ii)].
items.note: DWP.2: "Prove Corollaries3.8–3.9 ..." and "the actual trace formula". The vanishing of H²_c (no coinvariants of an open subgroup of Sp on the standard representation) is used implicitly.

items.name: Algebraicity of eigenvalues on H¹_c
items.statement: The left side Z(U₀,F₀,t) is a formal series with rational coefficients (by its product expansion and (iii)); the right side is therefore a polynomial with rational coefficients, of which 1/α is a root; hence α is algebraic.
items.note: DWP.2: "Include algebraicity from rational local factors".

items.name: Absolute convergence of the Euler product for |t| < q^{−β/2−1}
items.statement: Under (3.2), let N be the rank of ℱ and write det(1−F_x t,ℱ)=Π_{i=1}^N(1−α_{i,x}t), so |α_{i,x}|=q_x^(β/2). For |t|=q^(−β/2−1−ε), ε>0, and the given open U₀⊂P¹ over F_q, Σ_{i,x}|α_{i,x}t^deg(x)|=NΣ_x q_x^(−1−ε)≤NΣ_{n≥1}(q^n+1)q^(−n(1+ε))=N(Σ_{n≥1}q^(−nε)+Σ_{n≥1}q^(−n(1+ε)))<∞. Both series are geometric. Thus the Euler product is absolutely convergent and nonzero for |t|<q^(−β/2−1), and every zero 1/α of det(1−F*t,H¹_c(U,ℱ)) satisfies |1/α|≥q^(−β/2−1).
items.note: Implements existing E16 in DWP.2’s convergence proof. The P¹ rational-point count q^n+1 gives the bound actually needed; the original H¹_c group and convergence radius are unchanged.

tests.name: Deligne74.EulerProduct.projectivePuncture
tests.statement: For q=2 and U₀=P¹ minus the degree-two point X²+X+1, all three rational points remain. At ε=5 the sum is at least 3/64>1/31, disproving the affine-only bound; the corrected two-series upper bound is 1/31+1/63.

items.name: Closed-point count on the affine and projective lines
items.statement: For every n≥1, A¹(F_{q^n}) has q^n points and P¹(F_{q^n}) has q^n+1 points. Each degree-n closed point supplies n distinct F_{q^n}-points, so the number of degree-n closed points is at most q^n on A¹ and at most q^n+1 on P¹ and on every open U₀⊂P¹. In particular, the projective bound applies to the U₀ in (3.1).
items.note: The affine count is retained; the projective count implements existing E16 and supplies the convergence estimate. This missing elementary input remains routed once to DWP.2, with no new formalization claim.

items.name: Corollary 3.9: coarse two-sided bound on H¹(P¹, j_*F)
items.statement: Let j₀ be the inclusion of U₀ in P¹_{F_q}, j that of U in P¹, and α an eigenvalue of F* acting on H¹(P¹, j_*F). Then α is an algebraic number all of whose complex conjugates satisfy q^{(β+1)/2 − 1/2} ≤ |α| ≤ q^{(β+1)/2 + 1/2}.
items.note: DWP.2: "Prove Corollaries3.8–3.9 with their **coarse**, not final Weil II, weight intervals for H¹_c(U,F) and H¹(ℙ¹,j_*F)." Under the hypotheses of (3.2). Consumed in §6 (6.3) and §7.

items.name: H¹_c(U,F) → H¹(P¹, j_*F) is surjective
items.statement: A segment of the long cohomology sequence of the short exact sequence 0 → j_!F → j_*F → j_*F/j_!F → 0 (j_! = extension by zero) reads H¹_c(U,F) → H¹(P¹, j_*F) → 0. Hence every eigenvalue α of F* on H¹(P¹,j_*F) already occurs in H¹_c(U,F) and satisfies (3.8).
items.note: DWP.2: "Include algebraicity from rational local factors, absolute convergence of the Euler product and the boundary exact sequence." (j_*F/j_!F is punctual, so its H¹ vanishes.)

items.name: Lower bound in (3.9) via Poincaré duality
items.statement: Poincaré duality (2.12) ensures that q^{β+1}α^{−1} is also an eigenvalue [of F* on H¹(P¹,j_*F)], whence |q^{β+1}α^{−1}| ≤ q^{(β+1)/2 + 1/2}, and the corollary.
items.note: DWP.2 ("Prove Corollaries3.8–3.9") with the pairing ψ: F ≅ F^∨(−β) and (2.12) (§2); DWP.0: "the reciprocal pairing of eigenvalues induced by a Frobenius-equivariant perfect pairing".

items.name: Complex local Lefschetz setting
items.statement: Over C: let D = {z : |z|<1} be the unit disc, D* = D − {0}, and f: X → D a morphism of analytic spaces. Assume a) X is nonsingular and purely of dimension n+1; b) f is proper; c) f is smooth outside a point x of the special fiber X₀ = f^{−1}(0); d) at x, f has a nondegenerate quadratic point. Let t≠0 in D and X_t = f^{−1}(t) 'the' general fiber.
items.note: Complex-analytic (singular cohomology) statement. Not planned: LPV.2 only says "Verify the n mod 4 sign table against complex comparison" and "The complex Milnor-fiber comparison is an optional verification through PR196 ComplexComparison and SGA 7 XIV". The paper uses (4.1) only as motivation and for the signs in (4.3).

items.name: Complex specialization morphism
items.statement: α) specialization morphisms sp: H^i(X₀,Z) → H^i(X_t,Z): X₀ is a deformation retract of X, and sp is the composite H^i(X₀,Z) ≅← H^i(X,Z) → H^i(X_t,Z).
items.note: Complex-analytic (singular cohomology) statement. Not planned: LPV.2 only says "Verify the n mod 4 sign table against complex comparison" and "The complex Milnor-fiber comparison is an optional verification through PR196 ComplexComparison and SGA 7 XIV". The paper uses (4.1) only as motivation and for the signs in (4.3).

items.name: Complex monodromy transformation T
items.statement: β) monodromy transformations T: H^i(X_t,Z) → H^i(X_t,Z), describing the effect on singular cycles of X_t of 'turning t around 0'; it is the action on H^i(X_t,Z), fiber at t of the local system R^i f_*Z|D*, of the positive generator of π₁(D*,t).
items.note: Complex-analytic (singular cohomology) statement. Not planned: LPV.2 only says "Verify the n mod 4 sign table against complex comparison" and "The complex Milnor-fiber comparison is an optional verification through PR196 ComplexComparison and SGA 7 XIV". The paper uses (4.1) only as motivation and for the signs in (4.3).

items.name: Complex vanishing cycle δ
items.statement: Lefschetz theory describes α) and β) in terms of the vanishing cycle δ ∈ H^n(X_t,Z). This cycle is well defined up to sign.
items.note: Complex-analytic (singular cohomology) statement. Not planned: LPV.2 only says "Verify the n mod 4 sign table against complex comparison" and "The complex Milnor-fiber comparison is an optional verification through PR196 ComplexComparison and SGA 7 XIV". The paper uses (4.1) only as motivation and for the signs in (4.3).

items.name: Complex specialization is an isomorphism outside degrees n, n+1
items.statement: For i ≠ n, n+1: H^i(X₀,Z) ≅ H^i(X_t,Z).
items.note: Complex-analytic (singular cohomology) statement. Not planned: LPV.2 only says "Verify the n mod 4 sign table against complex comparison" and "The complex Milnor-fiber comparison is an optional verification through PR196 ComplexComparison and SGA 7 XIV". The paper uses (4.1) only as motivation and for the signs in (4.3).

items.name: Complex five-term exact sequence
items.statement: For i = n, n+1 there is an exact sequence 0 → H^n(X₀,Z) → H^n(X_t,Z) --(x ↦ (x,δ))--> Z → H^{n+1}(X₀,Z) → H^{n+1}(X_t,Z) → 0.
items.note: Complex-analytic (singular cohomology) statement. Not planned: LPV.2 only says "Verify the n mod 4 sign table against complex comparison" and "The complex Milnor-fiber comparison is an optional verification through PR196 ComplexComparison and SGA 7 XIV". The paper uses (4.1) only as motivation and for the signs in (4.3).

items.name: Complex Picard–Lefschetz formula
items.statement: For i ≠ n the monodromy T is the identity. For i = n, Tx = x ± (x,δ)δ.
items.note: Complex-analytic (singular cohomology) statement. Not planned: LPV.2 only says "Verify the n mod 4 sign table against complex comparison" and "The complex Milnor-fiber comparison is an optional verification through PR196 ComplexComparison and SGA 7 XIV". The paper uses (4.1) only as motivation and for the signs in (4.3).

items.name: Sign table for Picard–Lefschetz, (δ,δ) and Tδ
items.statement: The values of ±, of Tδ and of (δ,δ) are: n ≡ 0 mod 4: Tx = x − (x,δ)δ, (δ,δ) = 2, Tδ = −δ; n ≡ 1: sign −, (δ,δ) = 0, Tδ = δ; n ≡ 2: sign +, (δ,δ) = −2, Tδ = −δ; n ≡ 3: sign +, (δ,δ) = 0, Tδ = δ.
items.note: LPV.2: "Verify the n mod 4 sign table against complex comparison rather than choosing a convenient unrecorded sign." The signs are reused in (4.3) A), B). Checked: sign = (−1)^{(n+1)(n+2)/2}, (δ,δ) = (−1)^{n(n−1)/2}·2 for n even; table consistent (e.g. n≡0: δ−2δ=−δ).

items.name: Monodromy is a symplectic transvection (n odd) / orthogonal reflection (n even)
items.statement: The monodromy transformation T respects the intersection form Tr(x∪y) on H^n(X_t,Z). For n odd it is a symplectic transvection; for n even it is an orthogonal symmetry (reflection).
items.note: Complex-analytic (singular cohomology) statement. Not planned: LPV.2 only says "Verify the n mod 4 sign table against complex comparison" and "The complex Milnor-fiber comparison is an optional verification through PR196 ComplexComparison and SGA 7 XIV". The paper uses (4.1) only as motivation and for the signs in (4.3). The algebraic analogue (symplectic/symmetric distinction) is in LPV.4 ("with the symplectic/symmetric distinction in dimensions n odd/even") but only globally.

items.name: Algebraic local Lefschetz setting over a henselian trait
items.statement: Let A be a henselian discrete valuation ring with algebraically closed residue field, S = Spec A, η its generic point (spectrum of the fraction field), s its closed point, η̄ a geometric generic point (spectrum of an algebraic closure of the fraction field). Let f: X → S be a proper morphism with X regular, purely of dimension n+1, and f smooth except at one ordinary quadratic point x in the special fiber X_s. Let ℓ be a prime different from the residue characteristic p of S, and X_η̄ the geometric generic fiber.
items.note: LPV.2: "For a proper morphism from a regular (n+1)-dimensional trait scheme, smooth outside one ordinary quadratic singularity of the special fiber, prove ...".

items.name: Ordinary quadratic point (recalled from SGA 7)
items.statement: x is an ordinary quadratic point of the special fiber X_s [used without definition; the notion is that of SGA 7 XV: étale-locally the singularity is given by a quadratic form whose projective quadric is nonsingular].
items.note: LPV.2: "Define an ordinary quadratic singularity using the completed/étale local hypersurface equation and a smooth projective tangent quadric." Deligne uses the term without defining it.

items.name: ℓ-adic specialization morphism (4.2.1)
items.statement: sp: H^i(X_s,Q_ℓ) ≅← H^i(X,Q_ℓ) → H^i(X_η̄,Q_ℓ) [the first arrow an isomorphism by proper base change over the henselian S].
items.note: LPV.0: "Construct specialization and the triangle i*K→RΨ_f(j*K)→RΦ_f(K)→".

items.name: Inertia action on generic-fiber cohomology (4.2.2)
items.statement: The role of T is played by the action of the inertia group I = Gal(η̄/η), acting on H^i(X_η̄,Q_ℓ) by transport of structure (cf. (1.15)): I = Gal(η̄/η) → GL(H^i(X_η̄,Q_ℓ)).
items.note: LPV.0: "RΨ_f, with its continuous inertia action"; LPV.1: "Compare geometric actions on the nearby-cycle complex with the induced actions on cohomology." (Since the residue field is algebraically closed, I = Gal(η̄/η).)

items.name: Sheaves on a henselian trait are described by specialization data
items.statement: The data (4.2.1), (4.2.2) describe the sheaves R^i f_*Q_ℓ on S completely.
items.note: Standard description of (constructible) sheaves on a strictly henselian trait as triples (F_s, F_η̄ with I-action, I-equivariant sp: F_s → F_η̄). Searched atlas for "sheaves on a trait"/"henselian trait": LPV.0 constructs specialization but no stage states this equivalence. Used in (4.4).

items.name: ℓ-adic vanishing cycle δ (4.3.1)
items.statement: Put n = 2m for n even and n = 2m+1 for n odd. (4.2.1) and (4.2.2) are again described in terms of a vanishing cycle δ ∈ H^n(X_η̄,Q_ℓ)(m). This cycle is well defined up to sign.
items.note: LPV.2: "identify the rank-one vanishing module, its twist, variation pairing and orientation ambiguity."

items.name: Specialization is an isomorphism outside degrees n, n+1 (4.3.2)
items.statement: For i ≠ n, n+1: H^i(X_s,Q_ℓ) ≅ H^i(X_η̄,Q_ℓ).
items.note: LPV.2: "prove specialization is an isomorphism outside degrees n and n+1".

items.name: Five-term specialization exact sequence (4.3.3)
items.statement: For i = n, n+1 there is an exact sequence 0 → H^n(X_s,Q_ℓ) → H^n(X_η̄,Q_ℓ) --(x ↦ Tr(x∪δ))--> Q_ℓ(m−n) → H^{n+1}(X_s,Q_ℓ) → H^{n+1}(X_η̄,Q_ℓ) → 0.
items.note: LPV.2: "construct the exact five-term sequence in those degrees". Twist checked: x∪δ ∈ H^{2n}(X_η̄)(m), Tr to Q_ℓ(m−n).

items.name: Local monodromy is trivial outside the middle degree
items.statement: The action (4.2.2) of I (the local monodromy) is trivial if i ≠ n.
items.note: LPV.2 (specialization iso outside n, n+1 plus the five-term sequence); in degree n+1 H^{n+1}(X_η̄) is a quotient of H^{n+1}(X_s), on which I acts trivially. No separate phrase; covered by LPV.2's "prove specialization is an isomorphism outside degrees n and n+1 and construct the exact five-term sequence".

items.name: Tame character t_ℓ : I → Z_ℓ(1)
items.statement: There is a canonical homomorphism t_ℓ : I → Z_ℓ(1).
items.note: LPV.1: "Construct tame/wild inertia and the tame character t_ℓ:I→Z_ℓ(1) using the existing ramification and roots-of-unity APIs."

items.name: Picard–Lefschetz formula, n odd
items.statement: A) n odd. The action of σ∈I on H^n(X_η̄,Q_ℓ) is x ↦ x ± t_ℓ(σ)(x,δ)δ, with the sign ± the same as in (4.1).
items.note: LPV.2: "In the odd-n case prove the Picard–Lefschetz formula ρ(σ)x=x+ε_n t_ℓ(σ)⟨x,δ⟩δ, with ε_n fixed by the intersection/trace convention and the necessary twists." Twist check: (x,δ)∈Q_ℓ(m−n), t_ℓ(σ)∈Z_ℓ(1), δ in (m): total m−n+1+m = 0. This is the case used in §§5–7.

items.name: Picard–Lefschetz formula, n even (p ≠ 2)
items.statement: B) n even (this case will not be used). If p ≠ 2, there is a unique character of order two ε: I → {±1}, and σx = x if ε(σ) = 1, σx = x ± (x,δ)δ if ε(σ) = −1, the sign ± being the same as in (4.1).
items.note: LPV.2: "In the even-n tame branch prove the quadratic-character reflection formula under p≠2."

items.name: δ ≠ 0: R^i f_*Q_ℓ constant for i ≠ n
items.statement: If δ ≠ 0: for i ≠ n, the sheaf R^i f_*Q_ℓ is constant.
items.note: LPV.2 (local statement; follows from (4.3.2), (4.3.3) and trivial monodromy). The global analogue is LPV.4: "Prove the locally constant descriptions of R^i f_*Q_ℓ for i≠n in the nonzero case".

items.name: δ ≠ 0: R^n f_*Q_ℓ = j_*j^*R^n f_*Q_ℓ
items.statement: If δ ≠ 0: let j be the inclusion of η in S. Then R^n f_*Q_ℓ = j_*j^*R^n f_*Q_ℓ.
items.note: LPV.2 (consequence of the five-term sequence and the Picard–Lefschetz formula: the inertia invariants equal ker(x ↦ (x,δ)) = image of H^n(X_s)). No separate stage phrase; LPV.2 plans the ingredients.

items.name: δ = 0 only possible for n odd
items.statement: δ = 0 is an exceptional case; since (δ,δ) = ±2 for n even, it can only occur for n odd.
items.note: LPV.2: "Treat δ=0 explicitly".

items.name: δ = 0: R^i f_*Q_ℓ constant for i ≠ n+1
items.statement: If δ = 0: for i ≠ n+1, the sheaf R^i f_*Q_ℓ is constant.
items.note: LPV.2: "Treat δ=0 explicitly: the exceptional skyscraper contribution is in degree n+1, not a nonzero middle local system."

items.name: δ = 0: skyscraper exact sequence in degree n+1
items.statement: If δ = 0: let Q_ℓ(m−n)_s be the sheaf Q_ℓ(m−n) on {s}, extended by zero on S. There is an exact sequence 0 → Q_ℓ(m−n)_s → R^{n+1}f_*Q_ℓ → j_*j^*R^{n+1}f_*Q_ℓ → 0, where j_*j^*R^{n+1}f_*Q_ℓ is a constant sheaf.
items.note: LPV.2: "Treat δ=0 explicitly: the exceptional skyscraper contribution is in degree n+1". Global version in LPV.4 ("the separate degree-(n+1) skyscraper sequence when all vanishing cycles vanish").

items.name: Pencil of hyperplane sections with axis A and the diagram X <- X~ -> D
items.statement: Over C: let P be a projective space of dimension >= 1 and P-check the dual projective space, whose points parametrize the hyperplanes of P; H_t denotes the hyperplane defined by t in P-check. If A is a linear subspace of P of codimension 2, the hyperplanes containing A are parametrized by the points of a line D in P-check, the dual of A; the hyperplanes (H_t)_{t in D} form the pencil with axis A. Let X in P be a connected nonsingular projective variety of dimension n+1, and X~ in X x D the set of pairs (x,t) with x in H_t. The first and second projections give the diagram (5.1.1) X <-pi- X~ -f-> D, and the fibre of f at t in D is the hyperplane section X_t = X ∩ H_t.
items.note: LPV.3: 'Construct the dual projective space, incidence variety, conormal/dual variety, axis and pencil parameter line.' Stated over C in (5.1); transposed verbatim to algebraically closed k in (5.6). No Mathlib/Tau Ceti declaration: grep of declarations.tsv and TauCeti sources for Lefschetz/vanishing-cycle/pencil/dual-variety found nothing relevant (only unrelated transvection matrices).

items.name: For a general axis the pencil over C has only nondegenerate critical points
items.statement: Over C, with X fixed as in (5.1) and A sufficiently general: A) A is transverse to X, and X~ is obtained from X by blowing up A ∩ X; in particular X~ is nonsingular. B) There is a finite subset S of D and for each s in S a point x_s in X_s such that f is smooth outside the x_s. C) The x_s are nondegenerate critical points of f. Consequently for each s in S the local Lefschetz theory (4.1) applies to a small disc D_s around s and to f^{-1}(D_s).
items.note: Classical complex Lefschetz theory (cited to Lefschetz's book [2] in (5.13 A)). LPV.3 plans only the algebraic existence 'after a Veronese embedding of degree r≥2', and its blowup/smoothness part ('Identify the incidence total space with the blowup along the smooth codimension-two axis, prove the total space smooth'); the characteristic-0, r=1 generic-axis statement over C is not planned as such. Only motivational: the paper uses the algebraic version (5.7). No Mathlib/Tau Ceti declaration: grep of declarations.tsv and TauCeti sources for Lefschetz/vanishing-cycle/pencil/dual-variety found nothing relevant (only unrelated transvection matrices).

items.name: Loops around the critical values generate pi_1(U,u) (complex case)
items.statement: Over C put U = D - S, choose u in U and disjoint loops (gamma_s)_{s in S} based at u, gamma_s turning once around s. These loops generate the fundamental group pi_1(U,u), which acts on H^i(X_u, Z), the fibre at u of the local system R^i f_* Z | U.
items.note: Topological fact (D is a Riemann sphere, U = sphere minus finitely many points). The atlas plans only the algebraic tame analogue in LPV.5 ('Prove the required topological generation of the geometric monodromy image by those local operators'); no stage plans the topological statement.

items.name: Global vanishing cycles and the global Picard-Lefschetz formula (complex case)
items.statement: By the local theory (4.1), to each s in S corresponds a vanishing cycle delta_s in H^n(X_u, Z), depending on the choice of the gamma_s. For i != n the action of pi_1(U,u) on H^i(X_u, Z) is trivial. For i = n one has (5.2.1) gamma_s x = x ± (x, delta_s) delta_s, with the signs of (4.1).
items.note: LPV.4: 'Transport local vanishing cycles along explicit étale paths ... Prove the locally constant descriptions of R^i f_*Q_ℓ for i≠n'; local formula in LPV.2 ('prove the Picard–Lefschetz formula ρ(σ)x=x+ε_n t_ℓ(σ)⟨x,δ⟩δ'). The atlas plans the ℓ-adic version (5.8), not the Z-coefficient topological one; this is what the paper actually uses.

items.name: Vanishing part E of the middle cohomology
items.statement: E is the subspace of H^n(X_u, Q) (resp. H^n(X_u, Q_ℓ) in (5.8)) generated by the vanishing cycles delta_s, s in S (the vanishing part of the cohomology).
items.note: LPV.4: 'Define E as their span and prove independence of path choices as a monodromy-stable subspace, not independence of the individual oriented vectors.'

items.name: E is monodromy-stable and its orthogonal is the monodromy invariants
items.statement: Proposition (5.3). E is stable under the monodromy group pi_1(U,u). The orthogonal E^perp of E for the intersection form Tr(x ∪ y) is the subspace of monodromy invariants in H^n(X_u, Q). Proof: since the gamma_s generate the monodromy group, this is clear from (5.2.1).
items.note: LPV.5: 'Prove the required topological generation of the geometric monodromy image by those local operators, and thereby complete LPV.4's identification of E^⊥ with the global invariant subspace'; LPV.5 sources 'Deligne I 5.3–5.11'. Used (ℓ-adically, (5.8 a 3)) to show R^n f_*/E and E∩E^perp are geometrically constant in (6.4).

items.name: Dual variety X-check and incidence family Y -> P-check
items.statement: X-check in P-check is the dual variety of X: the set of t in P-check such that H_t is tangent to X, i.e. such that X_t is singular or X ⊂ H_t. Y in X x P-check is the space of pairs (x,t) with x in H_t, giving X <- Y -g-> P-check; the fibre of g at t is X_t = X ∩ H_t, and g is smooth outside the inverse image of X-check. Replacing P-check by a line D and Y by g^{-1}(D) recovers (5.1), with S = D ∩ X-check.
items.note: LPV.3: 'Construct the dual projective space, incidence variety, conormal/dual variety, axis and pencil parameter line.'

items.name: The dual variety is irreducible
items.statement: The dual variety X-check of the connected nonsingular projective X is irreducible.
items.note: Stated without proof ('La variété X-check est irréductible'): X-check is the image of the conormal variety, a projective bundle over the irreducible X. LPV.5: 'Prove conjugacy ... using the irreducible dual variety'; the conormal variety is in LPV.3. Used so that two points of the smooth locus of X-check can be joined inside that smooth locus.

items.name: Lefschetz/Bertini: pi_1(D - S) -> pi_1(P-check - X-check) is surjective for general D
items.statement: (Theorem of Lefschetz.) For D a sufficiently general line in P-check, the map pi_1(D - S, u) -> pi_1(P-check - X-check, u) is surjective. In the abstract setting (5.8) it is replaced by Bertini's theorem (for the tame fundamental group).
items.note: Recalled, not proved. LPV.5: 'using the irreducible dual variety and the required fundamental-group/Bertini surjectivity.'

items.name: Meridian loops around the dual variety are all conjugate
items.statement: For x in the smooth locus of codimension 1 of X-check, let ch be a path from t to x in P-check - X-check and gamma_x the loop following ch to near X-check, turning once around X-check, and returning along ch. The gamma_x (for variable ch) are conjugate to each other; since X-check is irreducible, the conjugacy class of gamma_x does not depend on x. In particular the gamma_s (s in S) are conjugate in pi_1(P-check - X-check). In the abstract setting one must invoke Abhyankar's lemma to control the ramification of R g_* Q_ℓ along the smooth codimension-one locus of X-check.
items.note: LPV.5: 'Construct the tame-cover specialization and Abhyankar-lemma argument controlling ramification along the smooth codimension-one dual locus. Do not transport the topological fundamental group argument without proving the algebraic tame comparison.'

items.name: The vanishing cycles are conjugate up to sign
items.statement: Theorem (5.4). The vanishing cycles ±delta_s (taken up to sign) are conjugate under the action of pi_1(U,u). Proof: by the surjectivity of pi_1(D-S) -> pi_1(P-check - X-check) it suffices to prove conjugacy under pi_1(P-check - X-check); the gamma_s are conjugate there, and by (5.2.1) this implies conjugacy of the ±delta_s.
items.note: LPV.5: 'Prove conjugacy, up to the orientation sign, of local vanishing cycles using the irreducible dual variety and the required fundamental-group/Bertini surjectivity.' Used in (5.5) and in (5.8 b) (if one vanishing cycle is 0, all are).

items.name: Absolute irreducibility of monodromy on E/(E ∩ E^perp)
items.statement: Corollary (5.5). The action of pi_1(U,u) on E/(E ∩ E^perp) is absolutely irreducible. Proof: let F ⊂ E ⊗ C be a monodromy-stable subspace. If F is not contained in (E ∩ E^perp) ⊗ C, there are x in F and s in S with (x, delta_s) != 0; then gamma_s x - x = ±(x,delta_s) delta_s lies in F, so delta_s in F; by (5.4) all delta_s lie in F, and F = E ⊗ C.
items.locator: §5, Cor. (5.5), p. 291; ℓ-adic version (5.8 a 3), p. 292
items.note: LPV.5: 'Prove absolute irreducibility of V=E/(E∩E^⊥) from the transvection generators and conjugacy.' Input to (5.10) via (5.11)(i). The print has "F = E" (PAPER-DELIGNE-74/E4).

items.name: Lefschetz pencil (abstract algebraic geometry)
items.statement: Let P be a projective space of dimension > 1 over an algebraically closed field k of characteristic p, and X ⊂ P a connected nonsingular projective variety of dimension n+1. For A a linear subspace of P of codimension 2 define D, the pencil (H_t)_{t in D}, the X_t, X~ and the diagram (5.1.1) as in (5.1). The (X_t)_{t in D} form a Lefschetz pencil of hyperplane sections if: A) the axis A is transverse to X (then X~ is the blow-up of X along A ∩ X and is smooth); B) there is a finite subset S of D and for each s in S a point x_s in X_s such that f is smooth outside the x_s; C) x_s is an ordinary quadratic singular point of X_s.
items.note: LPV.3: 'Identify the incidence total space with the blowup along the smooth codimension-two axis, prove the total space smooth, the morphism projective, and the singular-value set finite with one ordinary quadratic singularity in each singular fiber.' Ordinary quadratic singularity defined in LPV.2.

items.name: Local Lefschetz theory applies at each critical value
items.statement: For a Lefschetz pencil and each s in S, the local Lefschetz theory of §4 applies to the spectrum D_s of the henselization of the local ring of D at s, and to X~_{D_s} = X~ ×_D D_s.
items.note: LPV.2: 'For a proper morphism from a regular (n+1)-dimensional trait scheme, smooth outside one ordinary quadratic singularity of the special fiber, prove specialization is an isomorphism outside degrees n and n+1 ...'. Requires checking X~_{D_s} is regular, which follows from A).

items.name: Degree-r Veronese embedding iota_(r)
items.statement: Let N be the dimension of P and r >= 1 an integer; iota_(r) is the embedding of P into the projective space of dimension binom(N+r, N) - 1 whose homogeneous coordinates are the monomials of degree r in the homogeneous coordinates of P. The hyperplane sections of iota_(r)(P) are the degree-r hypersurfaces of P.
items.note: LPV.3: 'prove existence over an algebraically closed field after a Veronese embedding of degree r≥2 in the source's theorem'. Mathlib has no Veronese embedding (grep 'Veronese' in declarations.tsv: none).

items.name: Existence of Lefschetz pencils after a Veronese embedding of degree r >= 2
items.statement: If p != 0 it may happen that no pencil of hyperplane sections of X is a Lefschetz pencil. However, if r >= 2 and the given projective embedding iota_1 : X -> P is replaced by iota_r = iota_(r) ∘ iota_1, then in this new embedding every sufficiently general pencil is a Lefschetz pencil. Equivalently, for r >= 2, a sufficiently general pencil of degree-r hypersurface sections of X is a Lefschetz pencil. (Proved in SGA 7, XVII.)
items.note: LPV.3: 'Starting with a smooth projective geometrically connected X, prove existence over an algebraically closed field after a Veronese embedding of degree r≥2 ...; a particular original embedding need not admit a Lefschetz pencil in positive characteristic.' Consumed by (7.1) (and needed to complete (5.12)).

items.name: R^n f_* Q_ℓ is tamely ramified at the critical values
items.statement: For a Lefschetz pencil of hyperplane sections of X, excluding the case p = 2, n even; U = D - S, u in U, ℓ a prime != p: the local results of §4 show that R^n f_* Q_ℓ is tamely ramified at each s in S.
items.note: Follows from the Picard–Lefschetz formula of §4. LPV.2: 'In the odd-n case prove the Picard–Lefschetz formula ρ(σ)x=x+ε_n t_ℓ(σ)⟨x,δ⟩δ ... In the even-n tame branch prove the quadratic-character reflection formula under p≠2.'

items.name: Tame fundamental group of U is a quotient of the profinite completion of the topological one
items.statement: The tame fundamental group of U is a quotient of the profinite completion of the analogous transcendental fundamental group (lifting of tame coverings to characteristic 0 and Riemann's existence theorem). Hence the algebraic situation is entirely parallel to the transcendental one and Lefschetz's results transpose by standard arguments; in particular the image of pi_1(U,u) is topologically generated by the local monodromies at the s in S.
items.note: LPV.5: 'This is a specialized extension of PR196's finite étale Galois-category/Riemann-existence owners ... Prove the required topological generation of the geometric monodromy image by those local operators.' Grothendieck (SGA 1 XIII) tame specialization; recalled, not proved.

items.name: R^i f_* Q_ℓ is constant for i != n (nonzero vanishing cycles)
items.statement: (5.8 a) If the vanishing cycles are nonzero: 1) for i != n, the sheaf R^i f_* Q_ℓ on D is constant.
items.note: LPV.4: 'Prove the locally constant descriptions of R^i f_*Q_ℓ for i≠n in the nonzero case'. Local input (4.4 a 1). Used in (6.4) (R^i f_{0*}Q_ℓ, i≠n, geometrically constant) and §7.

items.name: R^n f_* Q_ℓ = j_* j^* R^n f_* Q_ℓ
items.statement: (5.8 a) If the vanishing cycles are nonzero: 2) with j the inclusion of U in D, R^n f_* Q_ℓ = j_* j^* R^n f_* Q_ℓ.
items.note: Global consequence of the local statement (4.4 a 2). LPV.2: 'prove specialization is an isomorphism outside degrees n and n+1 and construct the exact five-term sequence in those degrees'; LPV.4 plans the global middle-degree descriptions. Used in §7 (H^1(D, j_* ...)).

items.name: ℓ-adic E: stable, E^perp = invariants
items.statement: (5.8 a 3) Let E ⊂ H^n(X_u, Q_ℓ) be the subspace spanned by the vanishing cycles. It is stable under pi_1(U,u), and E^perp = H^n(X_u, Q_ℓ)^{pi_1(U,u)}.
items.note: LPV.5: 'and thereby complete LPV.4's identification of E^⊥ with the global invariant subspace'. ℓ-adic transposition of (5.3).

items.name: Absolute irreducibility and generation by transvections (ℓ-adic)
items.statement: (5.8 a 3) The representation of pi_1(U,u) on E/(E ∩ E^perp) is absolutely irreducible, and the image of pi_1 in GL(E/(E ∩ E^perp)) is (topologically) generated by the maps x -> x ± (x, delta_s) delta_s (s in S), the sign ± being determined as in (4.1).
items.note: LPV.5: 'Prove the required topological generation of the geometric monodromy image by those local operators ... Prove absolute irreducibility of V=E/(E∩E^⊥)'. (5.13 D): SGA 7 XVIII proves irreducibility only when E∩E^perp = {0}; the radical-quotient form avoids hard Lefschetz (needed to know E∩E^perp=0).

items.name: Case of zero vanishing cycles
items.statement: (5.8 b) If the vanishing cycles are zero (exceptional case; since (delta,delta) = ±2 for n even it can only occur for n odd, n = 2m+1; if one vanishing cycle is zero all are, being conjugate): 1) for i != n+1 the sheaf R^i f_* Q_ℓ is constant; 2) there is an exact sequence 0 -> ⊕_{s in S} Q_ℓ(m-n)_s -> R^{n+1} f_* Q_ℓ -> F -> 0 with F constant (Q_ℓ(m-n)_s the sheaf Q_ℓ(m-n) on {s} extended by zero); 3) E = 0.
items.note: LPV.4: 'and the separate degree-(n+1) skyscraper sequence when all vanishing cycles vanish'; LPV.2: 'Treat δ=0 explicitly: the exceptional skyscraper contribution is in degree n+1'. Used in §7.

items.name: Nondegenerate form psi on E/(E ∩ E^perp) and the monodromy representation rho
items.statement: The subspace E ∩ E^perp of E is the kernel of the restriction to E of the intersection form Tr(x ∪ y). This form therefore induces a nondegenerate bilinear form psi : E/(E∩E^perp) ⊗ E/(E∩E^perp) -> Q_ℓ(-n), alternating for n odd and symmetric for n even. It is respected by monodromy; for n odd the monodromy representation induces rho : pi_1(U,u) -> Sp(E/(E ∩ E^perp), psi).
items.note: LPV.4: 'Construct E^⊥ ... and prove the pairing descends nondegenerately to E/(E∩E^⊥), with the symplectic/symmetric distinction in dimensions n odd/even.' Only the symplectic (n odd) case is used; no orthogonal (n even) monodromy statement is made in the paper.

items.name: Kazhdan–Margulis: the monodromy image is open in Sp
items.statement: Theorem (5.10) (Kazhdan–Margulis). For n odd, the image of rho : pi_1(U,u) -> Sp(E/(E ∩ E^perp), psi) is open.
items.note: LPV.5: 'For odd n, prove that the compact monodromy image is **open** in Sp(V), not just Zariski dense.' Printed as 'Kajdan-Margulis'. Keyword search for Kazhdan/Margulis in the atlas finds only unrelated roadmaps (GeometryOfNumbers, EndoscopicTransfer). Consumed by (6.11) and (6.3) (hypothesis of (3.2)).

items.name: Image compact hence ℓ-adic analytic; openness reduces to Lie algebra = sp
items.statement: The image of rho is a compact, hence ℓ-adic analytic, subgroup of Sp(E/(E ∩ E^perp), psi). It suffices to show its Lie algebra L equals sp(E/(E ∩ E^perp), psi). (The transcendental analogue of L is the Lie algebra of the Zariski closure of the monodromy group.)
items.note: LPV.5: 'Build the necessary ℓ-adic analytic matrix-group/closed-subgroup and exponential-logarithm lemmas if unavailable ... deduce openness by the local analytic inverse-function/subgroup argument.' Cartan's closed-subgroup theorem for ℓ-adic Lie groups is not in Mathlib (no p-adic Lie group API found).

items.name: L is generated by square-zero N_s and E/(E∩E^perp) is an absolutely irreducible L-module
items.statement: From (5.8) it follows that L is generated by the square-zero transformations N_s : x -> (x, delta_s) delta_s (s in S), and that E/(E ∩ E^perp) is an absolutely irreducible representation of L. The theorem then follows from Lemma (5.11).
items.note: LPV.5: 'show its Q_ℓ-Lie algebra is generated by the square-zero operators x↦⟨x,δ⟩δ.' See PAPER-DELIGNE-74/E5: only 'L contains the Lie algebra generated by the N_s, which is irreducible' is needed.

items.name: Irreducible Lie subalgebra of sp generated by rank-one square-zero elements is sp
items.statement: Lemma (5.11). Let V be a finite-dimensional vector space over a field k of characteristic 0, psi a nondegenerate alternating form and L a Lie subalgebra of sp(V, psi). Assume: (i) V is a simple representation of L; (ii) L is generated by a family of endomorphisms of V of the form x -> psi(x, delta) delta. Then L = sp(V, psi).
items.note: LPV.5: 'Prove Deligne I 5.11: an irreducible symplectic Lie subalgebra generated by these operators is all sp(V)'. Tau Ceti has sp root generators (TauCeti/Algebra/Lie/Symplectic/StandardCarrier/Basic.lean, SpStd.rootGenerator) but no statement of this lemma; Mathlib has LieAlgebra.Symplectic.sp only as a definition.

items.name: Structure of W = {delta : N(delta) in L}
items.statement: In the setting of (5.11), with V (hence L) nonzero, let W = {delta in V : N(delta) : x -> psi(x,delta) delta lies in L}. a) W is stable under homotheties. b) If delta in W, exp(lambda N(delta)) is an automorphism of (V, psi, L), hence maps W to itself; for delta', delta'' in W, exp(lambda N(delta')).delta'' = delta'' + lambda psi(delta'', delta') delta' in W; if psi(delta', delta'') != 0 the subspace spanned by delta' and delta'' lies in W. c) Hence W is the union of its maximal linear subspaces W_alpha, which are pairwise orthogonal; each W_alpha is stable under the N(delta) (delta in W), hence under L; by (i), W_alpha = V and L contains all N(delta), delta in V.
items.note: Proof steps of Lemma 5.11, planned with it in LPV.5 ('Prove Deligne I 5.11').

items.name: sp(V,psi) is generated by the N(delta)
items.statement: For V finite-dimensional with nondegenerate alternating psi (characteristic 0), the Lie algebra sp(V, psi) is generated by the endomorphisms N(delta) : x -> psi(x, delta) delta, delta in V.
items.note: Final step of (5.11) ('On conclut en notant que ...'), planned with Deligne I 5.11 in LPV.5. In fact they span sp(V,psi) linearly (polarisation gives x -> psi(x,a)b + psi(x,b)a).
