Not found in Mathlib/Tau Ceti (searched declarations.tsv for LieAlgebra.Symplectic and SpStd span/generation lemmas).

items.name: Cohomology of a smooth odd-dimensional hypersurface outside the middle degree
items.statement: Let X_0 be a (smooth) hypersurface of odd dimension n in P^{n+1}_{F_q} and X_0-bar its extension of scalars to F_q-bar. Then H^{2i}(X_0-bar, Q_ℓ) = Q_ℓ(-i) for 0 <= i <= n; H^{2i}(X_0-bar, Q_ℓ(i)) is generated by the i-th cup power of eta = c_1(O(1)), the class of a hyperplane section. Hence Z(X_0, t) = det(1 - F* t, H^n(X_0-bar, Q_ℓ)) / prod_{i=0}^{n} (1 - q^i t), and det(1 - F* t, H^n(X_0-bar, Q_ℓ)) is a polynomial with integer coefficients independent of ℓ.
items.note: Stated without proof (weak Lefschetz for hypersurfaces). Searched atlas stage descriptions for 'hypersurface' (only unrelated hits: DerivedDeRham, CrystallineCohomology, LPV.2's local equation); no stage plans it. Remark marked 'inutile pour la suite'.

items.name: Sketch: Weil conjecture (1.6) for odd-dimensional hypersurfaces via a pencil of hypersurfaces
items.statement: Remark (5.12) (not used later). (1.6) is easy to prove for a hypersurface X_0 of odd dimension n in P^{n+1}_{F_q}: let X_0 vary in a Lefschetz pencil of hypersurfaces defined over F_q (cf. (5.7) for X = P^{n+1}; the existence of such a pencil is not clear, and completing the argument would require the arguments of (7.1)). One checks that E coincides with the whole H^n, and (3.2) gives the Weil conjecture for all hypersurfaces of the pencil, in particular for X_0.
items.note: Explicitly incomplete sketch (author flags the gap: existence of the pencil over F_q). Superseded by §7 / DWP.4; no atlas stage plans this special route.

items.name: Arithmetic Lefschetz pencil over F_q with X of even dimension
items.statement: Let P_0 be a projective space of dimension >= 1 over F_q, X_0 ⊂ P_0 a nonsingular projective variety, A_0 ⊂ P_0 a linear subspace of codimension two, D_0 ⊂ P_0-check the dual line, F_q-bar an algebraic closure of F_q, and P, X, A, D over F_q-bar deduced by extension of scalars. The diagram (5.1.1) of (5.6) comes from an analogous diagram (6.1.1) X_0 <-pi_0- X~_0 -f_0-> D_0 over F_q. Assume X connected of even dimension n+1 = 2m+2 and the pencil (X_t)_{t in D} defined by D a Lefschetz pencil. The set S of t in D with X_t singular is defined over F_q, i.e. comes from S_0 ⊂ D_0. Put U_0 = D_0 - S_0 and U = D - S.
items.note: DWP.3: 'For a Lefschetz pencil on a smooth projective variety of **even total dimension**, use LPV.5's odd-dimensional fiber monodromy ... Prove all Frobenius/descent compatibility'. Descent of S: LPV.3 'descend all finite-presentation data'.

items.name: The vanishing local system E and its descent E_0 ⊂ R^n f_{0*} Q_ℓ
items.statement: For u in U, E ⊂ H^n(X_u, Q_ℓ) is stable under pi_1(U,u), hence defines a local subsystem calE of R^n f_* Q_ℓ on U. R^i f_* Q_ℓ is the inverse image of the Q_ℓ-sheaf R^i f_{0*} Q_ℓ on D_0, and on U, calE is the inverse image of a local subsystem calE_0 ⊂ R^n f_{0*} Q_ℓ.
items.note: DWP.3: 'Construct the vanishing local system E, its orthogonal E⊥ in middle cohomology, the radical E∩E⊥ and the quotient E/(E∩E⊥). Prove all Frobenius/descent compatibility'. Descent holds because E is stable under the arithmetic fundamental group (Frobenius permutes the ±delta_s up to twist); the paper asserts it without comment.

items.name: Alternating pairing psi and perfect duality on calE_0/(calE_0 ∩ calE_0^perp)
items.statement: Cup product is an alternating form psi : R^n f_{0*} Q_ℓ ⊗ R^n f_{0*} Q_ℓ -> Q_ℓ(-n). With calE_0^perp the orthogonal of calE_0 for psi in R^n f_{0*} Q_ℓ | U_0, psi induces a perfect duality psi : calE_0/(calE_0 ∩ calE_0^perp) ⊗ calE_0/(calE_0 ∩ calE_0^perp) -> Q_ℓ(-n).
items.note: DWP.3: 'identify the alternating pairing and twist on this quotient.' Arithmetic version of (5.9).

items.name: Rationality of local characteristic polynomials of calE_0/(calE_0 ∩ calE_0^perp)
items.statement: Theorem (6.2). For every closed point x in |U_0|, the polynomial det(1 - F_x* t, calE_0/(calE_0 ∩ calE_0^perp)) has rational coefficients.
items.note: DWP.3: 'Prove **Weil I Theorem6.2**, rationality of every local characteristic polynomial of the quotient. This is not the already known rationality of the whole variety's zeta function.' Supplies the rationality hypothesis of (3.2) for (6.3).

items.name: Coarse weight bound for H^1(D, j_* calE/(calE ∩ calE^perp))
items.statement: Corollary (6.3). Let j_0 be the inclusion of U_0 in D_0 and j that of U in D. The eigenvalues of F* acting on H^1(D, j_*(calE/(calE ∩ calE^perp))) are algebraic numbers all of whose complex conjugates alpha satisfy q^{(n+1)/2 - 1/2} <= |alpha| <= q^{(n+1)/2 + 1/2}. Proof: by (5.10) and (6.2), the hypotheses of (3.2) hold for (U_0, calE_0/(calE_0 ∩ calE_0^perp), psi) with beta = n; apply (3.9).
items.note: DWP.3: 'Apply DWP.2 to obtain Corollary6.3 for H¹ of the quotient's j_* extension.' Uses (3.2)/(3.9) from §3 (DWP.2) and (5.10) (LPV.5). Consumed in (7.1).

items.name: Geometrically constant sheaves have Frobenius polynomials prod(1 - alpha_i^{deg x} t)
items.statement: Lemma (6.4). Let calG_0 be a twisted constant Q_ℓ-sheaf on U_0 whose inverse image calG on U is a constant sheaf. Then there are units alpha_i in Q_ℓ-bar such that for every x in |U_0|, det(1 - F_x* t, calG_0) = prod_i (1 - alpha_i^{deg(x)} t). (calG_0 is the inverse image of a sheaf on Spec(F_q), namely its direct image, which is an ℓ-adic representation G_0 of Gal(F_q-bar/F_q), and one takes det(1 - F t, G_0) = prod_i (1 - alpha_i t).)
items.note: DWP.3: 'Construct §6's comparison with geometrically constant factors, finite families of eigenvalues and their powers'. Uses that U is connected (geometrically connected U_0) so the direct image to Spec(F_q) pulls back isomorphically.

items.name: Lemma (6.4) applies to R^i f_{0*}Q_ℓ (i != n), R^n f_{0*}Q_ℓ/calE_0 and calE_0 ∩ calE_0^perp
items.statement: Lemma (6.4) applies to R^i f_{0*} Q_ℓ (i != n), to R^n f_{0*} Q_ℓ / calE_0 and to calE_0 ∩ calE_0^perp (restricted to U_0), i.e. these are geometrically constant.
items.note: Stated without proof; follows from (5.8 a 1) and (5.8 a 3): R^n/E is dual (via Poincaré duality on the fibre) to E^perp = invariants, and E∩E^perp ⊂ E^perp consists of invariants. DWP.3: 'Retain the radical and its geometrically constant terms: proving it is zero by hard Lefschetz would introduce a circular dependency.'

items.name: Zeta function of the fibres as Z^f times Z^m
items.statement: For x in |U_0|, the fibre X_x = f_0^{-1}(x) is a variety over the finite field k(x); for x-bar a point of U over x, X_{x-bar} is deduced from X_x by extension of scalars to k(x-bar) = F_q-bar, and H^i(X_{x-bar}, Q_ℓ) is the fibre of R^i f_* Q_ℓ at x-bar. Formula (1.5.4) for X_x over k(x) gives Z(X_x, t) = prod_i det(1 - F_x* t, R^i f_{0*} Q_ℓ)^{(-1)^{i+1}}, and Z(X_x, t) is the product of Z^f = det(1 - F_x* t, R^n f_{0*}Q_ℓ/calE_0) . det(1 - F_x* t, calE_0 ∩ calE_0^perp) . prod_{i != n} det(1 - F_x* t, R^i f_{0*}Q_ℓ)^{(-1)^{i+1}} by Z^m = det(1 - F_x* t, calE_0/(calE_0 ∩ calE_0^perp)).
items.note: Uses the Grothendieck trace formula (1.5.4) (from §1, PR196 TraceFormula) and proper base change; n is odd so the middle factor has exponent +1. DWP.3 dependency line: 'PR196 trace/rationality for the underlying varieties'; plan phrase 'Construct §6's comparison with geometrically constant factors'.

items.name: Z(X_x,t) = prod(1-alpha_i^{deg x} t)/prod(1-beta_j^{deg x} t) . det(1-F_x* t, calF_0) with alpha_i != beta_j
items.statement: Put calF_0 = calE_0/(calE_0 ∩ calE_0^perp) and calF = calE/(calE ∩ calE^perp). Applying (6.4) to the factors of Z^f, there exist ℓ-adic units alpha_i (1 <= i <= N) and beta_j (1 <= j <= M) in Q_ℓ-bar such that for every x in |U_0|, Z(X_x, t) = [prod_i (1 - alpha_i^{deg x} t) / prod_j (1 - beta_j^{deg x} t)] . det(1 - F_x* t, calF_0); in particular the right side lies in Q(t). Cancelling coinciding alpha_i = beta_j in pairs, one may and does assume alpha_i != beta_j for all i, j.
items.note: DWP.3: 'Prove the needed product/eigenvalue separation lemmas and the exceptional-root exclusions, retaining multiplicities'. Rationality of Z(X_x,t) in Q(t) is the Grothendieck/Dwork rationality (§1).

items.name: Reduction: it suffices that prod(1-alpha_i t) and prod(1-beta_j t) have rational coefficients
items.statement: (6.5) It suffices (for (6.2)) to prove that the polynomials prod_i (1 - alpha_i t) and prod_j (1 - beta_j t) have rational coefficients, i.e. that the family of the alpha_i (resp. of the beta_j) is defined over Q.
items.note: Then prod(1-alpha_i^{d}t), prod(1-beta_j^{d}t) are rational for every d, and det(1-F_x* t, calF_0) = Z(X_x,t) . prod(1-beta_j^{deg x}t)/prod(1-alpha_i^{deg x}t) is in Q(t) ∩ Q_ℓ[t]. Planned in DWP.3 ('Prove Weil I Theorem6.2').

items.name: Denominator of the twisted product is prod(1 - delta_j^{deg x} t) for most x
items.statement: Proposition (6.6). Let (gamma_i) (1 <= i <= P) and (delta_j) (1 <= j <= Q) be two families of ℓ-adic units in Q_ℓ-bar with gamma_i != delta_j. If K is a sufficiently large finite set of integers != 1 and L a sufficiently large density-0 subset of |U_0|, then for x in |U_0| with k ∤ deg(x) for all k in K and x not in L, the denominator of (6.6.1) det(1 - F_x* t, calF_0) prod_i (1 - gamma_i^{deg(x)} t) / prod_j (1 - delta_j^{deg(x)} t), written in lowest terms, is prod_j (1 - delta_j^{deg(x)} t).
items.note: DWP.3: 'Prove the needed product/eigenvalue separation lemmas and the exceptional-root exclusions, retaining multiplicities and finite base extension.' Gives an intrinsic description of the family delta_j via (6.7).

items.name: Families whose n-th powers agree for most n agree
items.statement: Lemma (6.7). Let K be a finite set of integers != 1, and (delta_j), (epsilon_j) (1 <= j <= Q) two families of elements of a field. If for every sufficiently large n not divisible by any k in K the family of the delta_j^n coincides with that of the epsilon_j^n (up to order), then the family of the delta_j coincides with that of the epsilon_j (up to order). Proof: induction on Q; the set of n with delta_Q^n = epsilon_j^n is an ideal (n_j); if delta_Q != epsilon_j for all j, all n_j != 1 and there are arbitrarily large n divisible by no n_j and no k in K, for which delta_Q^n != epsilon_j^n for all j, contradicting the hypothesis; so delta_Q = epsilon_{j_0} for some j_0, and one applies induction to (delta_j)_{j != Q}, (epsilon_j)_{j != j_0}.
items.note: DWP.3: 'finite families of eigenvalues and their powers'. Elementary; not in Mathlib (no multiset-of-powers injectivity lemma found). The integers of K are nonnegative in the application (the exponents n_ij ≥ 0 of (6.13)), so the printed condition '≠ 1' suffices there.

items.name: If prod(1-delta_j^{deg x}t) divides prod(1-gamma_i^{deg x}t).det(1-F_x* t, calF_0) for all x then S(t) | R(t)
items.statement: Proposition (6.8). Let (gamma_i) (1 <= i <= P) and (delta_j) (1 <= j <= Q) be two families of ℓ-adic units in Q_ℓ-bar, R(t) = prod_i (1 - gamma_i t), S(t) = prod_j (1 - delta_j t). Suppose that for all x in |U_0|, prod_j (1 - delta_j^{deg(x)} t) divides prod_i (1 - gamma_i^{deg(x)} t) . det(1 - F_x* t, calF_0). Then S(t) divides R(t). Proof: remove common pairs from (gamma_i), (delta_j) until the hypothesis of (6.6) holds; by (6.6) and the hypothesis, the fractions (6.6.1) are polynomials, so no delta remains, i.e. S | R.
items.note: Printed 'unités p-adiques' and '∏_i(1−δ_i^{deg(x)}t)'; see PAPER-DELIGNE-74/E6 and E7; the statement above is corrected. Planned with §6 in DWP.3.

items.name: Intrinsic characterisation of R(t) as an lcm
items.statement: Proposition (6.8) characterises R(t) intrinsically in terms of the family of polynomials prod_i (1 - gamma_i^{deg(x)} t) . det(1 - F_x* t, calF_0) (x in |U_0|): R(t) is the lcm of the polynomials S(t) = prod_j (1 - delta_j t) satisfying the hypothesis of (6.8).
items.note: Used in (6.9) to show the alpha_i family is defined over Q. Planned with §6 in DWP.3.

items.name: Proof of (6.5) and hence (6.2), modulo (6.6)
items.statement: (6.9) Apply (6.6) with (gamma_i) = (alpha_i), (delta_j) = (beta_j): one obtains (via (6.7)) an intrinsic characterisation of the family beta_j in terms of the rational functions Z(X_x, t) (x in |U_0|); since these lie in Q(t), the family beta_j is defined over Q. Then the polynomials prod_i (1 - alpha_i^{deg(x)} t) . det(1 - F_x* t, calF_0) lie in Q[t], and (6.8) gives an intrinsic description of the family alpha_i in terms of this family of polynomials; so the family alpha_i is defined over Q.
items.note: Galois-invariance argument: any automorphism of Q-bar (after embedding into Q_ℓ-bar) fixing the data permutes the family. DWP.3 plans Theorem 6.2's proof.

items.name: Arithmetic monodromy rho: pi_1(U_0,u) -> CSp(calF_u, psi), group H and rho_1
items.statement: In the setting of (6.1), let d be the fixed odd geometric dimension of the smooth fibers of the Lefschetz pencil (not the rank of ℱ_u), so the alternating pairing on the nonzero radical quotient ℱ_u has values in Q_ℓ(−d). Let a∈Ẑ denote the arithmetic degree, with arithmetic Frobenius φ:x↦x^q identified with +1. Arithmetic monodromy ρ:π₁(U₀,u)→CSp(ℱ_u,ψ) factors together with the degree projection through H={(a,g):μ(g)=q^(−da)} and ρ₁:π₁(U₀,u)→H. Powers q^a are defined continuously since q is an ℓ-adic unit. Geometric Frobenius F_x maps to −deg(x), so μ(ρ(F_x))=q^(d·deg(x)).
items.note: Implements existing E8 with distinct d and a. The pairing’s geometric degree d is fixed throughout 6.10–6.13; the Ẑ coordinate varies. DWP.3 owns this density argument.

items.name: pi_1(U_0,u) is an extension of Z-hat by pi_1(U,u)
items.statement: The arithmetic fundamental group pi_1(U_0, u) is an extension of Z-hat = Gal(F_q-bar/F_q) by the geometric fundamental group pi_1(U, u): pi_1(U, u) = Ker(pi_1(U_0, u) -> Z-hat) and pi_1(U_0,u) -> Z-hat is surjective.
items.note: Standard input (SGA 1 IX 6.1, geometrically connected U_0), recalled without proof. Searched atlas for 'homotopy exact sequence', 'fundamental exact sequence', 'geometric fundamental group': no stage plans it for varieties over finite fields (only BelyiMaps/function-field Langlands mentions). DWP.3 uses it implicitly.

items.name: The image H_1 of rho_1 is open in H
items.statement: In the corrected H={(a,g):μ(g)=q^(−da)} of (6.10), the compact image H₁=im(ρ₁) is open in H: it projects onto Ẑ and its intersection with ker(H→Ẑ)=Sp(ℱ_u,ψ) is open by (5.10). Its fibers over a are open subsets of the actual Sp-torsors CSp_a={g:μ(g)=q^(−da)}.
items.note: DWP.3. Openness uses the compact-image/open-geometric-kernel/surjective-degree argument; no replacement of q^(−da) by q^(−a) is made.

items.name: Frobenius-eigenvalue locus is closed of Haar measure zero
items.statement: In (6.10)–(6.11) with fixed odd pencil-fiber dimension d, let δ∈Q_ℓ-bar be an ℓ-adic unit and extend a↦δ^a continuously to a∈Ẑ in a finite coefficient extension containing δ. Then Z_δ={(a,g)∈H₁:det(g−δ^a I)=0} is closed and Haar-null. For each a define CSp_a={g:μ(g)=q^(−da)} and Z_a={g∈CSp_a:det(g−δ^a I)=0}. CSp_a is an Sp-torsor; Z_a is a proper algebraic zero locus after coefficient extension and is null for its invariant ℓ-adic analytic measure. Each H₁-fiber is open in that torsor, so its intersection with Z_a has conditional measure zero. Haar disintegration/Fubini for H₁→Ẑ proves that Z_δ has total measure zero.
items.note: Implements existing E8 in the actual fibers rather than the incorrect μ(g)=q^(−a) fibers. DWP.3 must supply the proper-algebraic-zero-locus measure lemma and Haar/Fubini interface. For 6.13 use Z_(δ_j^(-1)), because F_x has degree coordinate −deg(x). If the radical quotient is zero, its eigenvalue locus is empty and the density exclusion is immediate; the nonzero symplectic argument supplies the substantive case.

tests.name: Deligne74.Monodromy.fixedDimension
tests.statement: At d=3,a=1,q=2 the fiber multiplier is 1/8, not 1/2. A similitude diag(1,1/8) in a symplectic plane lies in the corrected multiplier torsor.

tests.name: Deligne74.Monodromy.geometricSign
tests.statement: For m=deg(x), a(F_x)=−m and (δ^(-1))^a=δ^m; the corrected fiber multiplier is q^(dm).

items.name: Proof of (6.6) via Chebotarev density
items.statement: For each i,j the positive integers r with γ_i^r=δ_j^r are multiples of a fixed integer n_ij (n_ij=0 denotes no positive solution), with n_ij≠1 under (6.6)’s hypothesis. By (6.12) applied to δ_j^(-1) and closed-point Chebotarev, the points x∈|U₀| for which some δ_j^deg(x) is an eigenvalue of geometric F_x on ℱ₀ have density zero: ρ₁(F_x) has a=−deg(x), so (δ_j^(-1))^a=δ_j^deg(x). Take K={n_ij} and L to be this exceptional set. The fixed odd pencil-fiber dimension d and H’s multipliers q^(−da) are unchanged throughout.
items.note: DWP.3. Retains the degree-congruence conditions and the existing E9 correction β_j→δ_j; applying 6.12 to the inverse unit matches the geometric-Frobenius convention of (1.15).

items.name: Chebotarev density for pi_1(U_0): Frobenii in a closed Haar-null subset of the image have density zero
items.statement: For the compact arithmetic image H₁ of the corrected ρ₁:π₁(U₀,u)→H={(a,g):μ(g)=q^(−da)}, function-field Chebotarev approximates conjugacy-invariant closed Haar-null sets by finite-quotient neighborhoods and shows that their geometric Frobenius points have Dirichlet density zero. Geometric F_x has degree coordinate −deg(x); retain constant-field degree-congruence restrictions in the finite quotients.
items.note: Recalled, not proved. DWP.3: 'Prove the stronger measure/density conclusion needed by6.13 ... by approximation with finite-quotient neighborhoods and the compatible closed-point Dirichlet-density statement.' Also FunctionFieldArithmetic:FA.5 plans 'a function-field Chebotarev statement retaining the congruence restriction on degrees'; DWP.3 is the specific owner.

items.name: Lemma 7.1: coarse Weil bound in even middle degree
items.statement: Let X_0 be a nonsingular, absolutely irreducible projective variety of even dimension d over F_q. Let X over \bar F_q be obtained from X_0 by extension of scalars and let α be an eigenvalue of F* acting on H^d(X, Q_ℓ). Then α is an algebraic number all of whose complex conjugates, again written α, satisfy (7.1.1) q^{d/2 − 1/2} ≤ |α| ≤ q^{d/2 + 1/2}. The proof is by induction on d (always even); the case d = 0 is trivial even without absolute irreducibility; from then on d ≥ 2 and one writes d = n + 1 = 2m + 2.
items.note: DWP.4: "Prove Weil I Lemma7.1 by induction on even dimension, with the intermediate bound q^(d/2−1/2)≤|α|≤q^(d/2+1/2) on middle cohomology." The key intermediate estimate of the paper; its error ±1/2 is removed in (7.3). Inputs: (5.7) Lefschetz pencils, (5.8) structure of R^i f_*, (2.10), (6.3) (the corollary of the fundamental estimate applied to the pencil), weak Lefschetz, blowup formula, Leray spectral sequence.

items.name: (7.1) is invariant under finite extension of F_q
items.statement: If F_{q^r} is an extension of degree r of F_q and X_0'/F_{q^r} is deduced from X_0/F_q by extension of scalars, then assertion (7.1) for X_0/F_q is equivalent to (7.1) for X_0'/F_{q^r}: q is replaced by q^r and the eigenvalues of F* are replaced by their r-th powers.
items.note: DWP.4: "Descend/extend the chosen projective embedding, pencil, singular values and vanishing cycles after a finite extension, and prove transfer back by taking powers of Frobenius." Used to assume the pencil and all its data are defined over F_q.

items.name: Rational Lefschetz pencil with rational singular points, vanishing cycles, base point and hyperplane section
items.statement: By (5.7), in a suitable projective embedding i: X → P, X admits a Lefschetz pencil of hyperplane sections; after a finite extension of F_q one may assume i and the pencil are defined over F_q, i.e. there are over F_q a projective embedding X_0 → P_0 and a codimension-two linear subspace A_0 of P_0 defining a Lefschetz pencil (notation of (6.1), (6.3): D, S, U, f: \tilde X → D). After a further extension of scalars one may assume: a) the points of S are defined over F_q; b) the vanishing cycles at x_s (s ∈ S) are defined over F_q (only ±δ is intrinsic, so a priori they are defined only over a quadratic extension); c) there is a rational point u_0 ∈ U_0, whose corresponding point u of U is taken as base point; d) X_{u_0} = f_0^{-1}(u_0) admits a smooth hyperplane section Y_0 defined over F_q; put Y = Y_0 ⊗_{F_q} \bar F_q.
items.note: LPV.3: "Over F_q, prove a nonempty admissible open has a point over some finite extension and descend all finite-presentation data. Do not assert it has an F_q-point. Give DWP.4 the exact base-extension/Frobenius-power interface used in Deligne I §7.1." Existence of the pencil is (5.7) (another section). Note the Lefschetz pencil here has odd fibre dimension n = d − 1, so the p = 2, n even exclusion of (5.8) does not arise.

items.name: Cohomology of the blowup along the pencil axis
items.statement: Since \tilde X is deduced from X by blowing up the smooth codimension-two subvariety A ∩ X, H^i(X, Q_ℓ) ↪ H^i(\tilde X, Q_ℓ) (in fact H^i(\tilde X, Q_ℓ) = H^i(X, Q_ℓ) ⊕ H^{i−2}(A ∩ X, Q_ℓ)(−1)), Frobenius-equivariantly. Hence it suffices to prove (7.1.1) for the eigenvalues of F* on H^d(\tilde X, Q_ℓ).
items.note: EDC.4: "Prove the projective-bundle decomposition through powers of c₁(O(1)), and the blowup formula along a smooth center, with pullback, exceptional Gysin, restriction and trace explicitly identified. Verify Tate twists and Frobenius on every summand ... Apply to the codimension-two axis of a pencil." Only the injectivity is used.

items.name: Leray reduction to the E_2 terms of the pencil
items.statement: The Leray spectral sequence for f: \tilde X → D is E_2^{pq} = H^p(D, R^q f_* Q_ℓ) ⇒ H^{p+q}(\tilde X, Q_ℓ). It suffices to prove (7.1.1) for the eigenvalues α of F* acting on the E_2^{pq} with p + q = d = n + 1, namely E_2^{2,n−1}, E_2^{0,n+1}, E_2^{1,n}.
items.note: DWP.4: "Use the blowup cohomology comparison and Leray spectral sequence. Analyze all three contributing terms H²(base,R^(d−2)), H¹(base,R^(d−1)) and H⁰(base,R^d) ... Subquotient weight bounds do not require degeneration or a splitting of that spectral sequence." Eigenvalues on the abutment are among those of the E_2 terms (subquotients); D is P^1 so only p = 0,1,2 occur.

items.name: Case A: the term E_2^{2,n−1}
items.statement: By (5.8), R^{n−1} f_* Q_ℓ is constant; by (2.10), E_2^{2,n−1} = H^{n−1}(X_u, Q_ℓ)(−1). By weak Lefschetz (corollary of SGA 4 XIV (3.2) and Poincaré duality SGA 4 XVIII), H^{n−1}(X_u, Q_ℓ)(−1) ↪ H^{n−1}(Y, Q_ℓ)(−1), and the induction hypothesis applies to Y_0 (smooth projective of even dimension n − 1 = d − 2).
items.note: DWP.4: "Prove Weil I Lemma7.1 by induction on even dimension, with the intermediate bound q^(d/2−1/2)≤|α|≤q^(d/2+1/2) on middle cohomology." and "Analyze all three contributing terms". (2.10) (H^2 of a constant sheaf on P^1 is the stalk twisted by (−1)) is in §2, outside this range. The induction hypothesis (7.1) is stated for absolutely irreducible varieties; the paper does not comment on this for Y_0. When d − 2 ≥ 2, Y is connected (smooth hyperplane section of the smooth connected fibre X_u, of dimension ≥ 3), and when d − 2 = 0 the d = 0 case was noted to hold without irreducibility, so nothing is lost.

items.name: Weak Lefschetz theorem (and its dual Gysin form)
items.statement: For X_u smooth projective of dimension n and Y a smooth hyperplane section, restriction H^{n−1}(X_u, Q_ℓ) → H^{n−1}(Y, Q_ℓ) is injective (corollary of SGA 4 XIV (3.2) together with Poincaré duality SGA 4 XVIII); dually the Gysin morphism H^{n−1}(Y, Q_ℓ)(−1) → H^{n+1}(X_u, Q_ℓ) is surjective. More generally (used in (7.2)⇒(1.7) d)) H^i(X) → H^i(Y) is injective for i < n.
items.note: EDC.4: "prove weak Lefschetz for a smooth hyperplane section Y of a smooth projective d-fold X: restriction is an isomorphism below d−1 and injective in degree d−1; prove its dual Gysin form." Standard input recalled from SGA 4.

items.name: Case B: the term E_2^{0,n+1}
items.statement: If the vanishing cycles are nonzero, R^{n+1} f_* Q_ℓ is constant and E_2^{0,n+1} = H^{n+1}(X_u, Q_ℓ); the Gysin morphism H^{n−1}(Y, Q_ℓ)(−1) → H^{n+1}(X_u, Q_ℓ) is surjective (dual to A)), and the induction hypothesis applies to Y_0. If the vanishing cycles are zero, the exact sequence of (5.8) b) gives an exact sequence ⊕_{s∈S} Q_ℓ(m−n) → E_2^{0,n+1} → H^{n+1}(X_u, Q_ℓ); the eigenvalue of F on Q_ℓ(m−n) is q^{d/2}, and H^{n+1} is treated as above.
items.note: DWP.4: "Prove Weil I Lemma7.1 by induction on even dimension, with the intermediate bound q^(d/2−1/2)≤|α|≤q^(d/2+1/2) on middle cohomology." and "including the zero vanishing-cycle case". Uses (5.8) a1), b2) (other section).

items.name: Case C: E_2^{1,n}, reduction to nonzero vanishing cycles and avoidance of hard Lefschetz
items.statement: If one had hard Lefschetz, E ∩ E^⊥ would be zero and R^n f_* Q_ℓ would be the direct sum of j_*E and a constant sheaf; H^1 of a constant sheaf on P^1 is zero and it would suffice to apply (6.3). Lacking hard Lefschetz, one dévisses. If the vanishing cycles are zero, R^n f_* Q_ℓ is constant ((5.8) b)) and E_2^{1,n} = 0. So one may assume the vanishing cycles nonzero, and filter R^n f_* Q_ℓ = j_* j^* R^n f_* Q_ℓ (5.8) by the subsheaves j_*E and j_*(E ∩ E^⊥).
items.note: DWP.4: "the nonzero-radical filtrations of §7.1" and "This stage does not use ... an invariant cycles result whose proof needs hard Lefschetz". Also DWP.3: "Retain the radical and its geometrically constant terms: proving it is zero by hard Lefschetz would introduce a circular dependency."

items.name: H^1 of a constant sheaf on P^1 vanishes
items.statement: Let k be algebraically closed of characteristic p≠ℓ. The early projective-bundle computation gives H⁰(P¹_k,Q_ℓ)=Q_ℓ, H¹(P¹_k,Q_ℓ)=0 and H²(P¹_k,Q_ℓ)=Q_ℓ(−1), with all other degrees zero; H¹(P¹_k,C)=0 for every finite-dimensional constant Q_ℓ-sheaf C by tensoring. When descended to F_q, geometric Frobenius acts by 1 in degree zero and q in degree two.
items.note: EDC.4 explicitly plans the projective-bundle decomposition via powers of c₁(O(1)), with Tate twists and Frobenius on every summand, independently of Weil bounds. DWP.4 and DWP.6 both import EDC.4. This supplies 7.1.2′, 7.1.4′ and 7.1.5′ before the Weil I induction, with no DWP.6→DWP.4 dependency.

items.name: Case C, first case: vanishing cycles not in E ∩ E^⊥
items.statement: If the vanishing cycles δ are not in E ∩ E^⊥, there are exact sequences (7.1.2) 0 → j_*E → R^n f_* Q_ℓ → constant sheaf → 0 and (7.1.3) 0 → constant sheaf j_*(E ∩ E^⊥) → j_*E → j_*(E/(E ∩ E^⊥)) → 0. The long exact cohomology sequences give (7.1.2') H^1(D, j_*E) → H^1(R^n f_* Q_ℓ) → 0 and (7.1.3') 0 → H^1(D, j_*E) → H^1(D, j_*(E/(E ∩ E^⊥))), and one applies (6.3).
items.note: DWP.4: "Prove Weil I Lemma7.1 by induction on even dimension, with the intermediate bound q^(d/2−1/2)≤|α|≤q^(d/2+1/2) on middle cohomology." and "the nonzero-radical filtrations of §7.1". (6.3) is DWP.3 ("Apply DWP.2 to obtain Corollary6.3 for H¹ of the quotient's j_* extension"). (7.1.3') uses H^0(D, j_*(E/(E∩E^⊥))) → H^1(constant)=0 so injectivity holds.

items.name: Case C, second case: vanishing cycles in E ∩ E^⊥
items.statement: If the δ lie in E ∩ E^⊥, then E ⊂ E^⊥ and there are exact sequences (7.1.4) 0 → the constant sheaf j_*E^⊥ → R^n f_* Q_ℓ → a sheaf ℱ → 0 and (7.1.5) 0 → ℱ → the constant sheaf j_*j^*ℱ → ⊕_{s∈S} Q_ℓ(m−n)_s → 0. The long exact sequences give (7.1.4') 0 → H^1(D, R^n f_* Q_ℓ) → H^1(D, ℱ) and (7.1.5') ⊕_{s∈S} Q_ℓ(m−n) → H^1(D, ℱ) → 0, and F acts on the skyscraper terms by multiplication by q^{d/2}.
items.note: DWP.4: "Prove Weil I Lemma7.1 by induction on even dimension, with the intermediate bound q^(d/2−1/2)≤|α|≤q^(d/2+1/2) on middle cohomology." The paper calls this case unwelcome ("à Dieu ne plaise"); it is a priori possible without hard Lefschetz. The print has Q_ℓ(n−m) for Q_ℓ(m−n) (PAPER-DELIGNE-74/E11); the statement above is corrected.

items.name: Lemma 7.2: purity in middle degree
items.statement: Let X_0 be a nonsingular absolutely irreducible projective variety of dimension d over F_q, X over \bar F_q deduced by extension of scalars, and α an eigenvalue of F* acting on H^d(X, Q_ℓ). Then α is an algebraic number all of whose complex conjugates, again written α, satisfy |α| = q^{d/2}.
items.note: DWP.4: "Apply Künneth to even Cartesian powers X^k: α^k occurs in middle degree kd, and the fixed half-unit error becomes 1/(2k). Prove the real-analysis limiting step to obtain |α|=q^(d/2), algebraicity and every complex conjugate". d here need not be even.

items.name: The assertion W(X_0, i)
items.statement: For X_0 projective nonsingular over F_q and i an integer, W(X_0, i) is the assertion: with X deduced from X_0 by extension of scalars from F_q to \bar F_q, every eigenvalue α of F* acting on H^i(X, Q_ℓ) is an algebraic number all of whose complex conjugates, again written α, satisfy |α| = q^{i/2}.
items.note: DWP.0 defines the Weil-number predicate ("Define Weil q-numbers of an integer weight on actual algebraic-number carriers and their all-embeddings absolute-value property"); DWP.4 exports "Weil I Lemma1.7 for every smooth projective X₀", i.e. W(X_0,i) for all i.

items.name: W(X_0,i) is invariant under finite base extension
items.statement: a) If F_{q^n} is an extension of degree n of F_q and X_0'/F_{q^n} is deduced from X_0/F_q by extension of scalars, then W(X_0, i) is equivalent to W(X_0', i): extending the scalars replaces α by α^n and q by q^n.
items.note: DWP.4: "handle components and finite-field descent"; DWP.0: "Prove ... finite-field base extension" for Weil numbers. Uses that |α^n| = q^{ni/2} for all conjugates iff |α| = q^{i/2}, and that α algebraic iff α^n algebraic.

items.name: W(X_0,i) ⇔ W(X_0,2n−i) by Poincaré duality
items.statement: b) If X_0 is purely of dimension n, W(X_0, i) is equivalent to W(X_0, 2n − i); this results from Poincaré duality.
items.note: DWP.4: "Reduce arbitrary cohomological degrees to middle degree by **weak** Lefschetz, duality and smooth hyperplane sections"; the pairing is EDC.2:pairings ("giving ⟨Fx,Fy⟩=q^d⟨x,y⟩"), and DWP.0 "the reciprocal pairing of eigenvalues induced by a Frobenius-equivariant perfect pairing". Eigenvalues pair as α ↔ q^n/α.

items.name: W is checked componentwise
items.statement: c) If X_0 is a sum (disjoint union) of varieties X_0^α, W(X_0, i) is equivalent to the conjunction of the W(X_0^α, i).
items.note: DWP.4: "handle components and finite-field descent". Combined with a) to pass to absolutely irreducible components (the geometric components of an irreducible X_0 become defined over a finite extension).

items.name: W(Y_0,i) ⇒ W(X_0,i) for i below the dimension
items.statement: d) If X_0 is purely of dimension n, Y_0 a smooth hyperplane section of X_0, and i < n, then W(Y_0, i) ⇒ W(X_0, i); this results from the weak Lefschetz theorem.
items.note: DWP.4: "Reduce arbitrary cohomological degrees to middle degree by **weak** Lefschetz, duality and smooth hyperplane sections"; weak Lefschetz is EDC.4. Existence of a smooth hyperplane section over F_q may require a finite extension (hence "par a) et d)").

items.name: (7.2) implies (1.7)
items.statement: (7.2) ⇒ (1.7): to prove W(X_0, i) for all projective nonsingular X_0 over F_q and all i, one reduces successively: by c), to X_0 purely of one dimension n; by b), to 0 ≤ i ≤ n; by a) and d), to i = n; by a) and c), to X_0 absolutely irreducible. This case is covered by (7.2).
items.note: DWP.4: "Export Weil I Lemma1.7 for every smooth projective X₀." The reduction by d) is an induction on n (hyperplane sections of lower dimension).

items.name: Frobenius eigenvalues on H^{kd}(X^k) include α^k
items.statement: For every integer k, if α is an eigenvalue of F* on H^d(X, Q_ℓ) then α^k is an eigenvalue of F* acting on H^{kd}(X^k, Q_ℓ) (Künneth formula).
items.note: DWP.4: "Apply Künneth to even Cartesian powers X^k: α^k occurs in middle degree kd". X^k is again nonsingular projective absolutely irreducible, of dimension kd (even for k even).

items.name: Proof of (7.2): removal of the error term by taking powers
items.statement: For k even, X^k satisfies the hypotheses of (7.1), whence q^{kd/2 − 1/2} ≤ |α^k| ≤ q^{kd/2 + 1/2} and q^{d/2 − 1/(2k)} ≤ |α| ≤ q^{d/2 + 1/(2k)} (for every complex conjugate). Letting k tend to infinity gives (7.2).
items.note: DWP.4: "the fixed half-unit error becomes 1/(2k). Prove the real-analysis limiting step to obtain |α|=q^(d/2), algebraicity and every complex conjugate, not just one chosen embedding." The printed upper bound in the first display has a sign misprint (PAPER-DELIGNE-74/E10); the statement above is corrected.

items.name: Theorem (1.7) (Riemann hypothesis for smooth projective varieties), proved
items.statement: For X_0 projective and nonsingular over F_q and every i, every eigenvalue α of F* on H^i(X, Q_ℓ) is an algebraic number all of whose complex conjugates satisfy |α| = q^{i/2} (i.e. W(X_0, i) holds). This completes the proof of (1.7), and with it (via the argument of §1, (1.7) ⇒ (1.6)) of the Weil conjectures (1.6).
items.note: DWP.4 exports (1.7); WC.3: "Import DWP.4's proved purity ... Follow Deligne I (1.7)⇒(1.6)". The deduction (1.7)⇒(1.6) itself is in §1 (outside this range).

items.name: Theorem 8.1: point counts of complete intersections
items.statement: Let X_0 ⊂ P_0^{n+r} be a nonsingular complete intersection over F_q, of dimension n and multidegree (d_1, …, d_r). Let b' be the n-th Betti number of the nonsingular complex complete intersections of the same dimension and multidegree. Put b = b' for n odd and b = b' − 1 for n even. Then |#X_0(F_q) − #P^n(F_q)| ≤ b·q^{n/2}.
items.note: Searched the atlas for "complete intersection", "hypersurface": no stage plans this. Closest: WC.5 plans the generic bound |N_r−(1+q^{dr})| ≤ Σ b_i q^{ir/2} (weaker, and for general varieties) and WC.4 plans the Betti-number comparison in families needed to identify dim H^n with the complex b'. Proof: trace formula (1.5) gives #X_0(F_q) = Σ_{i=0}^n q^i + (−1)^n Σ_j α_j with α_j the eigenvalues on primitive H^n; (1.7) gives |α_j| = q^{n/2}; triangle inequality. The proof prints #P(F_q) for #Pⁿ(F_q) (PAPER-DELIGNE-74/E12).

items.name: Cohomology of a smooth complete intersection
items.statement: For X/\bar F_q deduced from a nonsingular complete intersection X_0 of dimension n, let Q_ℓ·η^i be the line in H^{2i}(X, Q_ℓ) spanned by the i-th cup-power of the class of a hyperplane section; F* acts on it by q^i. The cohomology of X is the sum of the Q_ℓ·η^i (0 ≤ i ≤ n) and of the primitive part of H^n(X, Q_ℓ), of dimension b.
items.note: Stated without reference (standard: SGA 7 XI, weak Lefschetz for complete intersections plus specialization/comparison to complex Betti numbers, cf. WC.4 "Betti-number comparison in families"). No atlas stage plans the complete-intersection cohomology computation; EDC.3/EDC.4 plan cycle classes/c₁ and weak Lefschetz only.

items.name: Holomorphic modular (cusp, primitive) form on Γ_0(N) of weight k and character ε
items.statement: N ≥ 1, ε: (Z/N)^* → C^* a character, k ≥ 2. A modular form on Γ_0(N) of weight k and character ε is a holomorphic function f on the Poincaré upper half-plane X such that f((az+b)/(cz+d)) = ε(a)^{-1}(cz+d)^k f(z) for all (a b; c d) ∈ SL(2, Z) with c ≡ 0 (N) (plus holomorphy at the cusps). f is assumed cuspidal and primitive ("new" in the sense of Atkin–Lehner and Miyake), in particular an eigenvector of the Hecke operators T_p (p ∤ N); f = Σ_{n≥1} a_n q^n, q = e^{2πiz}, a_1 = 1.
items.note: Read TauCeti/NumberTheory/ModularForms/DiamondOperators.lean:279 (cuspFormCharSpace, diamond-eigenspace in S_k(Γ₁(N))) and :376 (mem_cuspFormCharSpace_iff_nebentypus: f∣[k]g = χ₀(d_g)•f for g∈Γ₀(N), with Gamma0Map = lower-right entry, Mathlib CongruenceSubgroups.lean:95); since ad ≡ 1 mod N, ε(a)^{-1} = ε(d), matching. Newforms: TauCeti.cuspFormsNew (Newforms/Basic.lean:200, Petersson-orthogonal complement of old forms); Hecke eigen: HeckeRing.GL2.IsEigenformAwayFromLevel (ModularForms/Eigenform.lean:65). The normalized primitive-form predicate (a_1 = 1, new AND eigen) is assembled from these; no single bundled declaration read.

items.name: Theorem 8.2: Ramanujan–Petersson conjecture for weight k ≥ 2
items.statement: Let N ≥ 1, ε: (Z/N)^* → C^* a character, k ≥ 2 and f a holomorphic modular form on Γ_0(N) of weight k and character ε, cuspidal and primitive, f = Σ a_n q^n with a_1 = 1. Then for p prime not dividing N, both roots of T^2 − a_p T + ε(p)·p^{k−1} have absolute value p^{(k−1)/2}, and consequently |a_p| ≤ 2·p^{(k−1)/2}.
items.note: AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations:R19.3: "Use the weight theorem R34 to prove purity and the coefficient-independent Frobenius polynomials. Construct the compatible family for a fixed eigenform"; WeightsInEtaleCohomology:R34.6 "Use DWP.10's export contracts in the existing eigenform/Kuga–Sato geometric realizations to deduce the actual eigenspace purity". Note the TauCeti ModularForms roadmap Layer 9 says explicitly "Proving Ramanujan–Deligne is **not a target**" there and uses the bound only as a hypothesis. The geometric eigenspace realization and purity prove both root moduli; α+β=a_p and the triangle inequality then give the trace bound. The reverse implication does not follow from α+β=a_p, αβ=ε(p)p^(k−1) and |ε(p)|=1 alone; it would require an independently justified normalized-reality relation. No such extra equivalence lemma is claimed here.

tests.name: Deligne74.Ramanujan.imaginaryTrace
tests.statement: For any r>0, ε=1, α=2ir and β=−ir/2 have αβ=r² and |α+β|=3r/2≤2r, but |α|=2r and |β|=r/2. A trace bound and determinant modulus alone do not imply root purity.

items.name: Hecke roots are Frobenius eigenvalues on H^{k−1} of a smooth projective (k−1)-fold (Deligne 1969)
items.statement: The roots of T^2 − a_p T + ε(p) p^{k−1} are eigenvalues of Frobenius acting on H^{k−1} of a nonsingular projective variety of dimension k − 1 defined over F_p. Under restrictive hypotheses this is proved in Deligne, Formes modulaires et représentations ℓ-adiques, Sém. Bourbaki exp. 355 (Feb. 1969), LNM 179; the general case is said to be not much harder.
items.note: AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations:R19.1: "Construct ... the higher-weight representation from symmetric-power cohomology or Kuga–Sato varieties. ... Prove the unramified characteristic polynomial by the geometric Eichler–Shimura relation." The paper requires a nonsingular projective model (desingularized Kuga–Sato variety over F_p, p ∤ N) — the general case is not proved in the paper (PAPER-DELIGNE-74/E15). Then (8.2) follows from (1.7) with i = k−1.

items.name: Remark 8.3: (8.2) holds for k = 1 (Deligne–Serre)
items.statement: J.-P. Serre and the author have recently proved that (8.2) remains true for k = 1. The proof is entirely different.
items.note: AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations:R19.1: "Construct the weight-one Artin representation in the Deligne–Serre setting needed for auxiliary arguments." The bound |a_p| ≤ 2 follows since a_p is the trace of a finite-order 2×2 matrix; this deduction is not stated explicitly in R19.1. Only announced here (no proof).

items.name: Theorem 8.4 (suggested by Bombieri): Deligne's bound for exponential sums of polynomials
items.statement: Let Q be a polynomial in n variables of degree d over F_q, Q_d its homogeneous part of degree d, and ψ: F_q → C^* a nontrivial additive character. Assume (i) d is prime to p; (ii) the hypersurface H_0 in P^{n−1}_{F_q} defined by Q_d is smooth. Then |Σ_{x_1,…,x_n ∈ F_q} ψ(Q(x_1,…,x_n))| ≤ (d − 1)^n q^{n/2}.
items.note: FiniteFieldsAndCharacterSums:FF.2: "State polynomial/rational exponential-sum bounds via curves and l-adic trace functions. Require the relevant nontriviality, conductor and purity conditions; import actual cohomological estimates from WeilConjectures and DeligneWeightsAndPurity." (FF.2 is a specification; it does not list the Artin–Schreier/Swan steps below.) There is no Kloosterman-sum application in this paper (Kloosterman sums are treated in SGA 4½); the only exponential-sum application is (8.4).

items.name: Reduction to the standard additive character
items.statement: Replacing Q by a scalar multiple, one may assume (8.4.1) ψ(x) = exp(2πi Tr_{F_q/F_p}(x)/p). (Every nontrivial additive character of F_q is x ↦ ψ_0(ax) for some a ∈ F_q^*, and aQ satisfies the same hypotheses with (aQ)_d = aQ_d.)
items.note: Mathlib has the ingredients but not the statement: AddChar.IsPrimitive.of_ne_one (NumberTheory/LegendreSymbol/AddCharacter.lean:84, nontrivial char of a field is primitive), AddChar.to_mulShift_inj_of_isPrimitive (:72, a ↦ ψ.mulShift a injective; the file comments that bijectivity is "left for a later occasion"), AddChar.card_eq (Analysis/Fourier/FiniteAbelian/PontryaginDuality.lean:101, card (AddChar α ℂ) = card α). Surjectivity follows by counting; the standard character is AddChar.FiniteField.primitiveChar (AddCharacter.lean:212) up to the trace normalization.

items.name: The Artin–Schreier covering X_0 → A_0 attached to Q
items.statement: Let X_0 be the étale covering of affine n-space A_0 over F_q with equation T^p − T = Q, σ: X_0 → A_0 the projection, X_0 = Spec(F_q[x_1, …, x_n, T]/(T^p − T − Q)). It is Galois with group Z/p; i ∈ Z/p = F_p acts by T ↦ T + i.
items.note: No atlas stage constructs the Artin–Schreier étale cover of A^n or its sheaf (AlgebraicCurves layer 10 has Artin–Schreier function-field covers y^p − y = u of curves, Stichtenoth III.7, not the étale-sheaf use). FF.2 mentions only "l-adic trace functions" generically.

items.name: Frobenius on the fibre of the Artin–Schreier cover is Tr(Q(x))
items.statement: Let x ∈ A_0(F_q), q = p^f. For (x, T) ∈ X_0(\bar F_q) above x, F((x, T)) = (x, T^q) and T^q = T + Σ_{i=1}^f (T^{p^i} − T^{p^{i−1}}) = T + Σ_i Q(x)^{p^{i−1}} = T + Tr_{F_q/F_p}(Q(x)). Thus Frobenius acts on the fibre of X_0/A_0 at x as the element Tr_{F_q/F_p}(Q(x)) of the Galois group.
items.note: Elementary finite-field computation; Mathlib has the finite-field trace as Algebra.trace and FiniteField Frobenius API, but I found no declaration identifying Tr_{F_q/F_p} with Σ x^{p^i} applied to Artin–Schreier roots (did not search exhaustively for the trace-as-sum-of-conjugates lemma). No atlas stage mentions it.

items.name: The rank-one λ-adic Artin–Schreier sheaves ℱ_{j,0}
items.statement: Let E be the field of p-th roots of unity and λ a finite place of E prime to p; work in λ-adic cohomology. For j ∈ Z/p, let ℱ_{j,0} be the E_λ-local system of rank one on A_0 defined by X_0 and ψ(−jx): Z/p → E^* → E_λ^*; one has ι: X_0 → ℱ_{j,0} with ι(i∗x) = ψ(−ji)ι(x). Objects without subscript 0 are those deduced by extension of scalars to \bar F_q.
items.note: No atlas stage constructs Artin–Schreier (Lang-torsor) sheaves; FF.2 speaks of "l-adic trace functions" but constructs nothing. Coefficients are E_λ (λ-adic), not Q_ℓ: the assembler should note (1.7) is used after ⊗E_λ.

items.name: Trace formula for the exponential sum
items.statement: The trace formula (1.12.1) for ℱ_{1,0} reads (8.4.2) Σ_{x_1,…,x_n ∈ F_q} ψ(Q(x_1, …, x_n)) = Σ_i (−1)^i Tr(F*, H^i_c(A, ℱ_1)).
items.note: FF.2: "State polynomial/rational exponential-sum bounds via curves and l-adic trace functions" and imports the trace formula. (1.12.1) (Grothendieck trace formula for compact support) is in §1, supplied by the external PR196 TraceFormula owner cited throughout the atlas. The text says "pour ℱ_{j,0}" but writes the j = 1 case (PAPER-DELIGNE-74/E13).

items.name: Decomposition of the cover's cohomology into character pieces
items.statement: σ_* E_λ = ⊕_j ℱ_j, and hence (8.4.3) H^*_c(X, Q_ℓ) ⊗_{Q_ℓ} E_λ = ⊕_j H^*_c(A, ℱ_j). For j = 0, ℱ_j is the constant sheaf E_λ; this factor corresponds to the inclusion, by pullback, of the cohomology of A into that of X.
items.note: Isotypic decomposition of a finite Galois (Z/p) pushforward; no atlas stage found. Here ℓ is the residue characteristic of λ.

items.name: Lemma 8.5 (i): cohomology of ℱ_j concentrated in degree n, dimension (d−1)^n
items.statement: For j ≠ 0, H^i_c(A, ℱ_j) is zero for i ≠ n; for i = n this cohomology space has dimension (d − 1)^n.
items.note: Not planned by any atlas stage (FF.2 is generic). Proved in (8.10)–(8.13): deformation to Σ x_i^d, Künneth, then n = 1 via Euler–Poincaré and Swan conductor.

items.name: Lemma 8.5 (ii): perfect duality between ℱ_j and ℱ_{−j}
items.statement: For j ≠ 0, the cup-product H^n_c(A, ℱ_j) ⊗ H^n_c(A, ℱ_{−j}) → H^{2n}_c(A, E_λ) →^{Tr} E_λ(−n) is a perfect duality.
items.note: Equivalent (by Poincaré duality, (2.8)/(2.12)) to H^n_c(A,ℱ_j) → H^n(A,ℱ_j) being an isomorphism (u_!ℱ_j = u_*ℱ_j, total wild ramification at ∞). Not in any atlas stage; EDC.2:pairings gives the underlying Poincaré duality.

items.name: Lemma 8.5 (iii): X_0 is open in a smooth projective Z_0
items.statement: X_0 is an open subset of a nonsingular projective variety Z_0 (and one can take Z_0 − X_0 a divisor with normal crossings, (8.9)).
items.note: Not planned. Proved in (8.6)–(8.9) by an explicit Zariski resolution; resolution of singularities in positive characteristic is not available in general, which is why the explicit local structure is needed.

items.name: Deduction of (8.4) from (8.5)
items.statement: Let j_0: X_0 ↪ Z_0 and j: X ↪ Z be deduced by extension of scalars to \bar F_q. By (8.4.2), (8.5)(i), and (1.7) for Z_0, it suffices to prove injectivity of H^n_c(A, ℱ_1) →^{σ*} H^n_c(X, ℱ_1) = H^n_c(X, E_λ) →^{j_!} H^n(Z, E_λ). One has Tr(a ∪ b) = (1/p) Tr(j_! σ* a ∪ j_! σ* b), so this injectivity results from (8.5)(ii).
items.note: Assembly step: H^n(Z) is pure of weight n by (1.7) (DWP.4) after ⊗E_λ, so the eigenvalues on H^n_c(A,ℱ_1) (dimension (d−1)^n) have absolute value q^{n/2}, and only degree n contributes to (8.4.2). The factor 1/p is the degree of σ. No atlas stage lists this argument; FF.2 plans only the headline bound.

items.name: Projective closure and normalization Y_0
items.statement: Let P_0 be the projective space over F_q completing A_0 by a hyperplane at infinity P_0^∞, H_0 ⊂ P_0^∞ the hypersurface with equation Q_d = 0, and Y_0 the normalization of P_0 in X_0. This gives the diagram (8.6.1): X_0 ↪ Y_0 over A_0 ↪ P_0 ↩ P_0^∞ ↩ H_0 (σ: X_0 → A_0, Y_0 → P_0). One studies Y_0/P_0 near infinity, étale-locally.
items.note: No atlas stage.

items.name: Lemma 8.7: Y_0 is smooth outside the inverse image of H_0
items.statement: Y_0 is smooth outside the inverse image of H_0. The divisor of the rational function Q on P_0 is the sum of its finite part div(Q)_f and −d times the hyperplane at infinity: (8.7.1) div(Q) = div(Q)_f − d P_0^∞, div(Q)_f ∩ P_0^∞ = H_0. At finite distance Y_0 = X_0 is étale over A_0, hence smooth. At infinity, outside the inverse image of H_0, there are local coordinates (z_1, …, z_n) with Q = z_1^{−d} (using (d, p) = 1); in these coordinates Y_0 is a product of a curve and a smooth space (coordinates z_2, …, z_n), hence smooth by normality.
items.note: No atlas stage. Local computation; uses hypothesis (i) (d,p)=1.

items.name: Lemma 8.8: over H_0, Y_0 is smooth over a fixed normal surface
items.statement: In an étale neighbourhood of a point above H_0, Y_0 is smooth over a singular normal surface, always the same one: there are local coordinates with Q = z_1^{−d} z_2 (since H_0 is smooth, div(Q)_f is smooth near infinity and meets P_0^∞ transversally); this form is independent of the chosen point and involves only two coordinates.
items.note: No atlas stage. Uses hypothesis (ii) (H_0 smooth).

items.name: Zariski's resolution procedure and the smooth compactification Z_0 with normal-crossings boundary
items.statement: The following procedure (due to Zariski) resolves the singularities of surfaces: alternately normalize and blow up the (reduced) singular locus. The operations commute with étale localization and with product by a smooth space, so the procedure also resolves spaces which, like Y_0, are étale-locally smooth over a surface; the resolution of Y_0 is the desired Z_0. Moreover, if T is a curve on a surface S containing the singular locus and T' its inverse image in the Zariski resolution S' of S, then iteratively blowing up in S' the (reduced) singular locus of (T')_red yields S'' in which the reduced inverse image (T'')_red of T is a divisor with normal crossings; since (Y_0, infinity) is étale-locally smooth over some (S, T), one can find Z_0 with Z_0 − X_0 a divisor with normal crossings.
items.note: Recalled as known ("On sait que"), no reference given. Atlas: StableReduction layer 4 plans Lipman-style resolution only for arithmetic surfaces (normal proper models of curves over a DVR), not Zariski's resolution of surfaces over a field nor the embedded normal-crossings step; AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry R09.7 is characteristic-zero Hironaka. So missing.

items.name: Universal family and relative compactification over the parameter space S
items.statement: Over \bar F_q, let S' be the affine space parametrizing polynomials in n variables of degree ≤ d, S ⊂ S' the open set of polynomials whose degree-d homogeneous part has nonzero discriminant, Q_S ∈ H^0(S, O_S[x_1, …, x_n]) the universal polynomial, X_S the étale Galois covering of A_S = A^n × S with equation T^p − T = Q_S (group Z/p), P_S = P^n × S, Y_S the normalization of P_S in X_S. The local expressions of (8.7), (8.8) remain valid with parameters, so étale-locally on Y_S, Y_S/S is isomorphic to the product of S (smooth) with a fibre; the canonical resolution of (8.9) gives a relative compactification Z_S/S of X_S/S with Z_S − X_S a divisor with relative normal crossings over S: u: X_S ↪ Z_S open, f: Z_S → S proper and smooth, σ: X_S → A_S, a: A_S → S.
items.note: No atlas stage.

items.name: Local constancy in the family; reduction to one polynomial
items.statement: Let ℱ_{j,S} be the E_λ-sheaf on A_S deduced as in (8.4) from X_S/A_S. Then σ_*E_λ = ⊕ ℱ_{j,S}, so R^*(fu)_!(E_λ) = ⊕_j R^* a_! ℱ_{j,S}. The properties of Z_S ensure that the R^i(fu)_! E_λ = R^i f_*(u_! E_λ) are locally constant sheaves on S; hence the R^i a_! ℱ_{j,S} are locally constant as well. Since S is connected, it suffices to prove (8.5)(i), (ii) for one particular polynomial Q; take Q = Σ_i x_i^d, which satisfies the nonsingularity condition because (d, p) = 1.
items.note: No atlas stage. Relies on local acyclicity/ lissité of R^i f_*(u_!Λ) for f proper smooth and u the complement of a relative NCD with constant (hence tame) coefficients (SGA 7 XIII / SGA 4½ Th. finitude-type input, not cited explicitly). Compatibility of the pairing in (ii) with the family is also implicitly used.

items.name: Künneth reduction to n = 1, Q = x^d
items.statement: For Q = Σ x_i^d the variables separate in the exponential sum of (8.4); correspondingly ℱ_j is the tensor product of the inverse images of analogous sheaves ℱ_j^1 on the one-dimensional factors A^1 of A = A^n, and by the Künneth formula H^•(A, ℱ_j) = ⊗ H^•(A^1, ℱ_j^1). This reduces the proof of (8.5)(i), (ii) to the case n = 1, Q = x^d.
items.note: Künneth for compact supports is imported by EDC.0 ("Import the already proved Rf! projection and Künneth formulas") from PR196; the Artin–Schreier sheaf factorization is not planned anywhere. Printed with H^• (no subscript c); since u_!ℱ_j = u_*ℱ_j both versions agree here.

items.name: Case n = 1: vanishing outside degree 1
items.statement: For n = 1 and Q = x^d, the covering X of A is irreducible, so for i = 0, 2, H^i_c(A, E_λ) ⥲ H^i_c(X, E_λ). Hence for i ≠ 1 and j ≠ 0, H^i_c(A, ℱ_j) = 0.
items.note: No atlas stage. Uses (8.4.3) with the j = 0 summand accounting for all of H^0_c, H^2_c.

items.name: Case n = 1: proof of (8.5)(ii)
items.statement: Assertion (ii) (for n = 1) results from (2.8) or (2.12) and from u_!ℱ_j = u_*ℱ_j (u the inclusion of A into P^1).
items.note: u_!ℱ_j = u_*ℱ_j because ℱ_j (j≠0) has no inertia invariants at ∞ (it is ramified there). (2.8)/(2.12) are the Poincaré duality statements of §2 (EDC.2:pairings). No atlas stage packages this.

items.name: Case n = 1: χ_c(A, ℱ_j) = 1 − d
items.statement: In the n=1 case Q=x^d, p∤d, and nontrivial Artin–Schreier character j, the imported general Grothendieck–Ogg–Shafarevich formula specializes to χ_c(A¹,ℱ_j)=rank(ℱ_j)(2−0−1)−Sw_∞(ℱ_j)=1−d using Lemma 8.12. Together with 8.11’s vanishing outside H¹_c this gives dim H¹_c=d−1.
items.note: FF.2 owns this Artin–Schreier application, not construction of the general genus-g GOS theorem. Reuse the existing FF packet’s shared EDC request and R01.3’s local Swan computation; the supplier’s ℓ-adic passage and proof closure belong to its étale-duality blueprint.

items.name: Grothendieck–Ogg–Shafarevich (Euler–Poincaré) formula
items.statement: Let k be algebraically closed of characteristic p, ℓ≠p, C/k a smooth projective connected curve of genus g, D⊂C a finite set of geometric points, U=C∖D and ℱ a finite-rank lisse E_λ-sheaf on U, where E_λ is a finite extension of Q_ℓ. Then χ_c(U,ℱ)=rank(ℱ)(2−2g−|D|)−Σ_{x∈D}Sw_x(ℱ). The genus and puncture terms are part of the general formula, not specialized away.
items.note: General supplier requested once in the étale-duality direction by RT-AREA-finitefields/3 (confirmed) and the existing FiniteFieldsAndCharacterSums packet’s EDC.2 request. Route 6 carries the proposal for that same owner; EDC.2:euler-characteristic is only a proposed substage, not registered/planned or proved. FF.2 imports it for 8.11. ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.3 remains the separate equal-characteristic local-conductor supplier.

items.name: Lemma 8.12: Swan conductor of ℱ_j at infinity
items.statement: The Swan conductor of ℱ_j (j ≠ 0, n = 1, Q = x^d) at infinity is equal to d.
items.note: Swan conductors are planned in ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations R01.3 ("Define conductors using the ramification filtration") but not this computation. Equivalent to (8.13) (Artin conductor = Swan + 1 for a totally ramified nontrivial character).

items.name: Lemma 8.13: conductor of an Artin–Schreier character
items.statement: Let k be a finite field of characteristic p, y ∈ k[[x]] an element of valuation d prime to p, L the extension of K = k((x)) generated by the roots of T^p − T = y^{−1}, and χ the character of Gal(L/K) with values in Z/p given by χ(σ) = σT − T. Then χ has conductor d + 1. Proof: by extension of the residue field reduce to k algebraically closed and apply Serre, Sur les corps locaux à corps résiduel algébriquement clos, Bull. SMF 89 (1961), 105–154, n° 4.4.
items.note: Not planned: searched "Artin–Schreier" (LocalFieldsRamification uses it only for unit filtrations at 2; AlgebraicCurves layer 7/10 has the different of Artin–Schreier function-field extensions, Stichtenoth III.7.8, which gives d(P′|P) = (p−1)(m+1) and hence the same conductor via the conductor–discriminant formula, but no stage states the conductor of the character).

routes.reason: Weil I is the source of the zeta-function definitions WC.1 exposes (the Hasse–Weil zeta function (1.1.1) of a scheme of finite type over Z, of which Z(X₀, t) is the finite-field case) and of the first worked application of the Riemann hypothesis to point counts: Theorem (8.1) bounds #X₀(F_q) for a smooth complete intersection by the primitive Betti number times q^{n/2}, using the cohomology of complete intersections (SGA 7 XI). That is exactly WC.5's point-count estimate specialised to complete intersections, where only the middle primitive cohomology survives; WC.5 should state (8.1) as a worked corollary.

DWP.2 and DWP.3 receive four missing proof inputs: Zariski density of an open subgroup of Sp(Q_ℓ), H⁰_c vanishing on an affine curve, the closed-point counts for A¹ and P¹, and the arithmetic/geometric fundamental exact sequence. For (3.8), use #P¹(F_{q^n})=q^n+1 and the two convergent geometric series in the corrected estimate, implementing E16 on the original open U₀⊂P¹. For (6.10)–(6.13), use the fixed odd pencil-fiber dimension d, arithmetic degree a, multiplier q^(−da) and geometric F_x coordinate −deg(x), so 6.12 is applied to δ_j^(-1). These suppliers serve the existing DWP.2/3 owners.

§§4–5 of Weil I are the classical recall of Lefschetz theory that LPV plans. The complex-analytic model of (4.1) (specialization, monodromy, vanishing cycle, five-term sequence, Picard–Lefschetz formula, transvection/reflection) is the comparison LPV.2 asks for when it says 'Verify the n mod 4 sign table against complex comparison'; the description of sheaves on a henselian trait by specialization data (4.2) belongs to LPV.0's nearby-cycle setup; the complex general-axis statement (5.1) and the generation of π₁ by loops around the critical values (5.2) are the complex counterparts of LPV.3's pencil existence and LPV.4's global vanishing cycles; and Remark (5.12) (hypersurface cohomology outside the middle degree, and the sketch of the Weil conjecture for odd-dimensional hypersurfaces through a pencil of hypersurfaces) is a worked instance for LPV.4.

FF.2 owns the Artin–Schreier constructions and applications of Bombieri’s (8.4): its sheaves and trace formula, (8.5) cohomology concentration/duality, (8.6)–(8.9) compactification, deformation/local constancy and Künneth reduction, and the n=1 application χ_c(A¹,ℱ_j)=1−d. It imports the general genus-g Grothendieck–Ogg–Shafarevich theorem from the shared étale-duality request carried by route 6, and the local Artin–Schreier Swan computation from R01.3 via route 5. It must not construct another general GOS theorem. The original polynomial hypotheses (p∤d and smooth leading form) remain unchanged.

Lemmas (8.12)–(8.13) compute a Swan conductor: the character of an Artin–Schreier extension T^p − T = y⁻¹ with v(y) = d prime to p has conductor d + 1, so ℱ_j has Swan conductor d at infinity. R01.3 plans Artin and Swan conductors from the ramification filtration; this computation is its natural worked example (Serre, Corps locaux à corps résiduel algébriquement clos, 1961, n° 4.4).

sourceIssues.locator: §5, proof of Théorème (5.10), printed p. 293, paragraph beginning « On déduit de (5.8) » (published text, Numdam scan)
sourceIssues.printed: The proof claims (5.8) shows that 𝔏 is generated by the square-zero transformations N_s : x ↦ (x, δ_s)δ_s (s ∈ S), with E/(E∩E^⊥) an absolutely irreducible representation of 𝔏. It then derives the theorem from the next lemma.
sourceIssues.correction: (5.8) only gives that 𝔏 contains the N_s: the unipotent generators exp(±N_s) lie in the compact image, and so does exp(Z_ℓ·N_s). Let 𝔏' ⊂ 𝔏 be the Lie algebra generated by the N_s. A subspace stable under 𝔏' is stable under every exp(λN_s), hence under the topological generators of the monodromy group, so 𝔏' acts absolutely irreducibly by (5.8). Lemma (5.11) applied to 𝔏' gives 𝔏' = 𝔰𝔭, and therefore 𝔏 = 𝔰𝔭.
sourceIssues.reason: For an ℓ-adic analytic group topologically generated by elements exp(N_s), it does not follow formally that its Lie algebra is generated by the N_s. Unlike the real case, the closed subgroup generated by exp(Z_ℓN_s) can be larger than the analytic subgroup of the algebra they generate. The equality is true a posteriori (both algebras equal 𝔰𝔭), and the repair above is immediate. So this is a real but harmless gap: the stated deduction is not valid as written.

review.reason: Rejected. The deduction is a standard one, not a gap. The image of ρ lies in the Q_ℓ-points of the algebraic subgroup H of Sp generated by the unipotent groups exp(G_a·N_s); in characteristic 0 the Lie algebra of such a group is the Lie algebra generated by the N_s (Chevalley: the Lie algebra generated by algebraic Lie subalgebras is algebraic). A closed subgroup of H(Q_ℓ) has Lie algebra inside Lie(H), so 𝔏 ⊆ ⟨N_s⟩; conversely each exp(Z_ℓ·N_s) lies in the image, so N_s ∈ 𝔏. Hence 𝔏 is exactly the Lie algebra generated by the N_s, as Deligne says, and the sentence before the display points to the Zariski closure for this reason. The reason given here ('the closed subgroup generated by exp(Z_ℓN_s) can be larger than the analytic subgroup of the algebra they generate') is false in this situation. The extraction's alternative argument is also valid; nothing in the paper changes.

sourceIssues.locator: §6, (6.10) Préliminaires, printed p. 298, lines 1–6 (definition of H); same convention in (6.12) « μ(g) = q^{−n} » (published text, Numdam scan)
sourceIssues.printed: The source defines H ⊂ Ẑ × CSp(ℱ_u, ψ) by q^{−n} = μ(g). It says q is an ℓ-adic unit, so qⁿ ∈ Q_ℓ* is defined for every n ∈ Ẑ. Since ψ takes values in Q_ℓ(−n), it claims that the map from π₁ to Ẑ × CSp, with coordinates the canonical projection to Ẑ and ρ, factors through ρ₁ : π₁(U₀, u) → H.
sourceIssues.correction: H = {(a, g) ∈ Ẑ × CSp(ℱ_u, ψ) : μ(g) = q^{−na}}, where n = dim of the fibres and a ∈ Ẑ is a separate letter. Correspondingly, in (6.12), CSp_a = {g : μ(g) = q^{−na}}.
sourceIssues.reason: In §6, n is the fibre dimension (X has dimension n+1, and ψ is the cup product with values in Q_ℓ(−n)). The equation uses n also for the Ẑ-coordinate. The generator φ (arithmetic Frobenius) acts on Q_ℓ(1) by q (§2), so an element over a ∈ Ẑ acts on Q_ℓ(−n) by q^{−na}. With the equation as printed, μ = q^{−a}, and ρ₁ would not land in H unless n = 1. With the corrected H, the proofs of (6.11)–(6.13) go through word for word: CSp_a is still an Sp-torsor, Ker(H → Ẑ) = Sp, and F_x lies over −deg(x), so (6.12) is applied to δ^{−1}, which is again an ℓ-adic unit.

sourceIssues.locator: §8, (8.11), printed p. 306 (u was defined in (8.10), p. 305) (published text, Numdam scan)
sourceIssues.printed: The diagram in (8.10) uses X_S ↪(u) Z_S, with f proper and smooth and u an open immersion. In (8.11), assertion (ii) is said to follow from (2.8) or (2.12), together with u_!ℱ_j = u_*ℱ_j.
sourceIssues.correction: In (8.11), u must denote the open immersion A = A¹ ↪ P¹ (the j of (2.11)–(2.12)), e.g. « … et de ce que, u désignant l'inclusion de A dans P¹, u_!ℱ_j = u_*ℱ_j ».
sourceIssues.reason: ℱ_j is a sheaf on A, so u_!ℱ_j only makes sense for an embedding of A. In the case n = 1 the relevant fact is that ℱ_j (j ≠ 0) is ramified at ∞, so its extension by zero and its direct image to P¹ coincide. Then (2.12) gives the duality (8.5)(ii). The letter u was defined just before, in (8.10), as the different map X_S ↪ Z_S, and it is not redefined.

sourceIssues.locator: §8, proof of Théorème (8.2) (Ramanujan–Petersson), printed p. 302 (published text, Numdam scan)
sourceIssues.printed: The source identifies these roots as Frobenius eigenvalues on H^{k−1} of a smooth projective variety over F_p of dimension k−1. It cites its Bourbaki talk on modular forms and ℓ-adic representations, exposé 355, February 1969, in volume 179 of Lecture Notes in Mathematics, for a proof under restrictive assumptions, and describes the general case as only slightly harder.
sourceIssues.correction: The key geometric input for general N, ε, k ≥ 2 and p ∤ N needs a proof. This means a smooth projective model over F_p (a smooth compactification of the Kuga–Sato variety, with an auxiliary level structure if needed) whose H^{k−1} contains the roots of T² − a_pT + ε(p)p^{k−1} as Frobenius eigenvalues, together with a Hecke/character projector. This was later supplied in the literature, e.g. by A. J. Scholl, « Motives for modular forms », Invent. Math. 100 (1990).
sourceIssues.reason: The theorem is stated in full generality, but the paper says explicitly that the needed geometric fact is proved in the cited exposé only under restrictive hypotheses. The general case is dismissed with « n'est pas beaucoup plus difficile » and no argument. The result is true, but its proof in the paper is incomplete for general (N, ε, k).

sourceIssues.locator: §3, proof of Corollaire (3.8), printed p. 286, the count of closed points (published text, Numdam scan); page image checked
sourceIssues.printed: The source counts qⁿ points of the affine line over F_{qⁿ}, and hence at most qⁿ closed points of degree n. It deduces Σ_x q_x^{−1−ε} ≤ Σ_n qⁿ.q^{n(−1−ε)} = Σ_n q^{−nε} < ∞.
sourceIssues.correction: U₀ is an open of P¹, so count on P¹: at most qⁿ + 1 closed points of degree n (at most qⁿ for n ≥ 2), giving Σ_x q_x^{−1−ε} ≤ Σ_n (qⁿ + 1)q^{n(−1−ε)} < ∞.
sourceIssues.reason: In (3.1) U₀ is the complement in P¹ of a finite set of closed points, and the reduction after (3.2) only makes U affine; it need not lie in the affine line. Example: q = 2, U₀ = P¹ minus the closed point x² + x + 1 = 0 (affine). The three rational points lie in U₀, and for ε = 5 they alone give Σ_x q_x^{−1−ε} ≥ 3·2^{−6} = 3/64, while Σ_n qⁿ·q^{n(−1−ε)} = Σ_n 2^{−5n} = 1/31 < 3/64; so the displayed inequality fails. Shrinking U₀ is not available here, since (3.8) is a statement about H¹_c(U, ℱ) for the given U. With the count on P¹ the series still converges, so (3.8) is unaffected.
